postings.title: 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting
postings.location: San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

We are looking for a Senior Manager, 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting to join our Accounting team. You will own revenue recognition, month-end close and reporting for Claude sold through our cloud service provider (CSP) channels: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. These channels are among the fastest-growing revenue streams at the company. They run on consumption-based, partner-reported data that changes every month.

You will be the accounting point of contact for the finance and partner teams at AWS, Google and Microsoft. Internally, you will partner with Finance, FAB, Engineering and business teams to turn partner billing feeds into accurate, auditable revenue. You will also lead the automation of a close that is still heavily manual. If you want to build the financial infrastructure behind a fast-growing AI company, come join us in our mission to build safe, beneficial AI.

Key responsibilities

- 

Lead the revenue close for cloud service provider Marketplace within a listed company timeline.

- 

Prepare and review revenue, revenue-share, reserve journal entries, accruals and true-ups including memos for accounting assessments and judgments.

- 

Own balance sheet reconciliations, reserves, and the usage-to-invoice-to-cash bridge.

- 

Perform monthly and quarterly flux analysis and prepare flux decks for leadership.

- 

Own quarter-end deliverables, including footnote disclosures, flux commentary and presentations to leadership and Corporate Accounting.

- 

Serve as the primary contact for external auditors.

- 

Review the work of accountants and contractors, set the close calendar, and keep close packages complete and audit-ready.

- 

Own monthly and quarterly 3P revenue reporting for leadership and FP&A, by partner, model, product, region and customer.

- 

Review partner usage, invoice, disbursement and fraud reports each month, and resolve data issues before close.

- 

Serve as the accounting point of contact for the finance, engineering and product teams and drive reporting improvements that support an on-time close.

- 

Apply ASC 606 to 3P arrangements, including principal-vs-agent, variable consideration and reseller arrangements.

- 

Estimate and document reserves, including credit loss (ASC 326).

- 

Assess the accounting for new 3P products, programs and billing changes, partnering with Technical Accounting on complex judgments.

- 

Partner with the Engineering teams to automate manual close processes, including SQL-driven workbooks, automated reconciliations and system-generated journal entries.

- 

Own 3P SOX controls, including design, documentation, gap remediation and audit evidence.

- 

Partner with FP&A, Treasury, AR and business teams on forecasts, cash and partner disputes.

Minimum qualifications

- 

Have strong ASC 606 knowledge, especially principal-vs-agent, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, and consumption-based revenue.

- 

Have owned a month-end close with tight deadlines and reviewed journal entries, reconciliations and flux analysis.

- 

Have built revenue reporting from large, imperfect third-party data sets and reconciled it to the general ledger.

- 

Have managed external partner relationships where you depended on their data, and pushed for fixes.

- 

Have strong SQL skills (BigQuery or similar) and experience automating close workbooks or reconciliations.

- 

Have designed or operated SOX controls and supported external audits.

- 

Communicate clearly with accounting, finance, business and engineering teams.

- 

Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built.

Preferred qualifications

- Have 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 3+ years managing revenue accounting or close teams.

- 

A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent (ACA, ACCA).

- 

Big 4 audit experience combined with industry experience at a high-growth tech or SaaS company.

- 

Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller or channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace).

- 

Experience with usage-based and subscription revenue models.

- 

Hands-on experience with Workday Financials, NetSuite, Numeric, Hex or similar close and reporting tools.

- 

Experience with IPO readiness.

- 

Experience using AI tools to automate accounting and reporting work.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.
Annual Salary:
$190,000—$230,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. postings.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the Role

Anthropic runs one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry, across multiple accelerator families, CPU families, clouds, neoclouds, and on-prem sites. Capacity Engineering owns the data, tooling, and systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization of that fleet: we partner on supply deals, wire telemetry from day zero, own the canonical capacity data layer, and build the planning and enforcement tools every research and product team relies on. This role sits in the Planning pillar, on the Demand Planning team, and works daily with research engineering, pretraining, inference, compute supply, finance, and external vendors.

You own the tranches. The job has two halves that feed each other. Upstream, you take the Demand Planning forecast and turn it into per-tranche requirements — shape, interconnect, region, supporting resources, date — and carry those into sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews so we contract for capacity we can actually use when we need it. Downstream, you own the integrated schedule and system of record for every tranche in flight — from contracted through reserved, ingested, in-cluster, healthy, and occupied — and you drive the owners of each hop to their dates. Every slip you see downstream becomes a contract-language fix, an automation, or a correction fed back to the forecast.

What you'll do

- Turn the forecast into per-tranche requirements. Take the Demand Planning forecast plus direct input from research, pretraining, and inference planners, and convert it into concrete accelerator, interconnect, region, supporting-resource, and date requirements for each tranche. Represent those in sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews, including which contractual terms actually move delivery dates.

- Qualify tranches for deliverability before signature. The Capacity Planner signs fit-to-forecast; you sign whether the shape can land schedulable, healthy, and instrumented in that region on that date, with storage, egress, identity in place.

- Close the delivery loop. Track forecast-versus-delivered on shape, region, and timing for every tranche; publish the variance; and feed it back to Demand Planning and into the next contract.

- Own the bring-up system of record. Define the canonical contract-to-occupied state machine with explicit entry and exit criteria per stage, and make it a first-class object in the capacity data layer so every downstream tool sees in-flight capacity, not only what has landed.

- Run a portfolio of bring-ups in parallel — new cloud regions, on-prem sites, neocloud blocks — with one integrated schedule spanning provider milestones, cluster creation, network turn-up, storage readiness, health burn-in, and first-workload landing. 

- Drive readiness automation: All capacity systems are fully integrated for all new capacity, from contracted through ingested, automated and scaled.

- Instrument and publish the numbers that matter — time-to-occupied and paid-idle dollars per tranche — with executive-level reporting on status, tradeoffs, and risk across the portfolio.

What you bring

- Significant experience delivering large-scale infrastructure — cloud regions, accelerator clusters, HPC systems, or bare-metal fleets — at multi-region scale or ≥10k accelerators (or CPU/storage equivalent).

- Technical range from through cluster orchestration and node health, up to the telemetry and planning tables on top — enough to debug where they disagree rather than route it.

- SQL and enough Python to answer your own questions and build your own reporting.

- A degree in a technical field or an equivalent engineering track record.

Preferred

- Reserved-capacity onboarding, private offers, or capacity commitments with cloud or neocloud providers.

- Enough demand-planning exposure to challenge a forecast, translate it into per-tranche requirements, and feed delivery variance back into it.

- Data center or colocation delivery: power and space planning, network turn-up, site acceptance, vendor management.

- Accelerator health and burn-in, collective-communications sanity testing, or fleet-health SLOs — and a rigorous definition of "healthy."

- Systems of record or lifecycle services for infrastructure assets.

- Onboarding a new hardware generation into an existing scheduler and observability stack.

postings.location: London, UK; Ontario, CAN; Remote-Friendly, United States; San Francisco, CA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
Applications are now open for our January cohort - apply here by October 30.

Anthropic Fellows Program overview

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on an empirical project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.

What to expect

- 4 months of full-time research 

- Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers 

- Access to a shared workspace (in either Bay Area, California, Toronto, Canada, or London, UK)

- Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community

- Weekly stipend of 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR + benefits (these vary by country)

- Funding for compute (~$15k/month) and other research expenses

Interview process

The interview process will include an initial application & reference check, technical assessments & interviews, and a research discussion. 

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Compensation

The expected base stipend for this role is 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension).

Across the workstreams, you may be a good fit if you:

- Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole

- Are excited to transition into empirical AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic

- Have a strong technical background in computer science, mathematics, or physics

- Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments

- Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Strong candidates may also have:

- Strong background in a discipline relevant to a specific Fellows workstream (e.g. economics, social sciences, or cybersecurity)

- Experience in areas of research or engineering related to their workstream

Candidates must be:

- Fluent in Python programming

- Available to work full-time on the Fellows program

AI Safety Fellows

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include:

- Sam Bowman

- Sara Price

- Alex Tamkin

- Nina Panickssery

- Trenton Bricken

- Logan Graham

- Jascha Sohl-Dickstein

- Joe Benton

- Collin Burns

- Fabien Roger

- Samuel Marks

- Kyle Fish

- Ethan Perez

Our mentors will lead projects in select AI safety research areas, such as:

- Scalable Oversight: Developing techniques to keep highly capable models helpful and honest, even as they surpass human-level intelligence in various domains.

- Adversarial Robustness and AI Control: Creating methods to ensure advanced AI systems remain safe and harmless in unfamiliar or adversarial scenarios.

- Model Organisms: Creating model organisms of misalignment to improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise.

- Model Internals / Mechanistic Interpretability: Advancing our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures.

- AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations.

On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about past projects, including:

- Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data: Alex Cloud and Minh Le, et al., mentors including Samuel Marks and Owain Evans

- Open-source circuits: Michael Hanna and Mateusz Piotrowski with mentorship from Emmanuel Ameisen and Jack Lindsey

For a full list of representative projects for each area, please see these blog posts: Introducing the Anthropic Fellows Program for AI Safety Research, Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions.

Unique candidate criteria

You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:

- Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems

- Have experience with empirical ML research projects

- Have experience working with large language models

- Have experience in one of the research areas mentioned above

- Have a track record of open-source contributions

AI Security Fellows

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include:

- Nicholas Carlini

- Keri Warr

- Evyatar Ben Asher

- Keane Lucas

- Newton Cheng

On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about some past Fellows projects, including:

- AI agents find $4.6M in blockchain smart contract exploits: Winnie Xiao and Cole Killian, mentored by Nicholas Carlini and Alwin Peng

- Strengthening Red Teams: A Modular Scaffold for Control Evaluations: Chloe Loughridge et al., mentored by Jon Kutasov and Joe Benton

Unique candidate criteria

You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:

- Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems

- Have contributed to open-source projects in LLM- or security-adjacent repositories

- Have demonstrated success in bringing clarity and ownership to ambiguous technical problems

- Have experience with pentesting, vulnerability research, or other offensive security work

- Have a demonstrated willingness to do the "dirty work" that produces high-quality outputs

- Have reported CVEs or been awarded bug bounties

- Have experience with empirical ML research projects

- Have experience with deep learning frameworks and experiment management

Logistics Requirements: To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program.

Workspace Locations: We have designated shared workspaces in London and Berkeley where fellows will work from and mentors will visit. We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada. We will ask you about your availability to work from Berkeley or London (full- or part-time) during the program.

Visa Sponsorship: We are not currently able to sponsor visas for fellows. To participate in the Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the UK, the US, or Canada.

Program Duration: The program runs for 4 months, full-time. If you can't commit to the full duration, please still apply and note your constraints in the application. We review these requests on a case-by-case basis.

Please note: We do not guarantee that we will make any full-time offers to fellows. However, strong performance during the program may indicate that a Fellow would be a good fit for full-time roles at Anthropic. We're looking for an Applied AI Architect to join Beneficial Deployments, focused on helping nonprofits and research institutes in APAC get real value from Claude. You'll be the technical lead for a portfolio of partners, working alongside our Account Executives from first conversation through deployment, and you'll support a wider set of accounts through learning sessions. With nonprofits, you'll find where Claude makes a real difference to their mission and their operations. With research institutes, you'll help researchers and the teams who support them use Claude in work they can check and stand behind. You'll design solutions that fit each partner's budget, data and teams, and turn early pilots into lasting adoption. What works for one partner becomes something others across the region and beyond can use.

Responsibilities

- Serve as the primary technical advisor to a portfolio of nonprofits and research institutes from discovery through deployment, turning their priorities into scoped use cases with clear measures of success.

- Partner with Account Executives on account plans, discovery and technical evaluation.

- Design and demo solutions with Claude, the API and Claude Code and Science for nonprofits and research institutes

- Help researchers evaluate Claude on their own questions and data before they rely on it, and be plain about its limits.

- Guide partners through security review, data governance and procurement, including rules that differ by country and limits on how research data can be used.

- Support a wider portfolio of accounts through learning sessions and enablement.

- Run workshops and trainings that build AI fluency across partner teams, from program staff to research groups.

- Build reusable assets (reference designs, connectors, prompt and eval templates) so one partner's work helps the next.

- Spot patterns across partners, bring field insight back to Product and Research, and help partners measure what changed.

- Travel up to 30% to partner sites for workshops, technical deep dives and relationship building.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have

- 7-10 years in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, sales engineering, forward-deployed engineering or technical consulting.

- A track record of getting lean, skeptical or slow-moving teams with many stakeholders to adopt technology and keep using it, including working through how they buy and govern it.

- Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs: you have built and evaluated working prototypes or agents, and can guide a partner's own engineers on architecture and evals. You don't need to write production code.

- The ability to earn the trust of researchers and other specialists: you can show how you tested something, where it fails and what you don't know yet.

- Clear written and spoken communication across a broad audience. The ability to explain technical tradeoffs to program leads, researchers, operations staff and executives.

- Patience with long buying and partnership cycles, a knack for knowing how to make them go smoothly, and real care for public benefit.

- A track record of agency and autonomy: you spot what needs doing before anyone asks, agree that it matters, drive it to a finished result and know when to pull others in.

- Comfort operating in ambiguity: you bring clarity to fuzzy problems, wear multiple hats and do whatever it takes to further the mission.

- Bonus if you've worked with or at nonprofits, foundations, research institutes or other mission-driven organizations, worked in a sales team, built multilingual products, or worked with partners in more than one country.

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

About the role

As an Applied AI Engineer on the Commercial team at Anthropic, you will be a trusted technical advisor to the companies that run the real economy, across software, financial services, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, and professional services, as they go from using Claude to building on it. Commercial is one of Anthropic's largest and fastest-moving books of business, covering thousands of mid-market and small companies. Some of these companies put Claude inside the product they sell, and others put agents to work inside their own engineering, operations, finance, and support teams, and this role works with both. You'll lead deep technical engagements, partnering directly with customer engineering teams to take their hardest agent builds from idea to production on the Claude API, the Agent SDK, Claude Managed Agents, Claude Code, and Claude for Enterprise. Many of these teams are lean, with years of existing systems and no dedicated AI function, and you will bridge the gap between what Claude can do and what it takes to run it inside a business that already has customers depending on it.

Working closely with Applied AI Architects, Account Executives, and Anthropic's Product, Engineering, and Research teams, you'll go deep where hands-on engineering changes the outcome, then turn what you learn into something the rest of the book can use. You'll leverage your AI engineering expertise to develop custom evaluation frameworks, design scalable architectures, and create the reference implementations, tooling, and technical resources that enable Commercial customers to succeed with Claude.

Responsibilities

- Serve as a deep technical advisor to high-potential Commercial customers, whether Claude sits inside the product they sell or inside the way they run their own business, bringing them use cases worth building and pushing the boundaries of what agents can do in engineering, operations, finance, customer support, and more

- Work hands-on with customer engineering teams through build sprints, pair programming, and architecture reviews that move agents from idea to production, and understand their stack, data, and workflows end to end so that your guidance fits the systems, security requirements, and team they have today

- Ship working code. Develop prototypes, near-production examples, and technical documentation, including evaluation suites that become the customer's acceptance criteria, AI engineering techniques, and architecture diagrams, that enable customers to build, operate, and scale with Claude

- Create reference implementations, blueprints, and sample code that many companies can adopt without starting from scratch, for example multi-agent systems on the Agent SDK or Claude Managed Agents, MCP servers for common business systems, or Claude Code running across the software development lifecycle

- Collaborate closely with Applied AI Architects and Account Executives to decide where engineering depth changes the outcome, and to maintain context and continuity across customer engagements

- Identify patterns across engagements, including what is hard about running agents inside established companies such as legacy systems, messy data, permissions and security review, cost and latency at scale, and model migrations, then build repeatable evaluations and solutions and contribute insights back to Product, Engineering, Research, and the broader Applied AI team

- Create technical content for customer and partner engineering audiences including documentation, tutorials, and sample code

- Foster community engagement through hackathons, webinars, technical office hours, and customer events

- Travel to customer sites for workshops, implementation guidance, and relationship building

You may be a good fit if you have

- Deep software engineering experience, gained by designing, building, and operating production systems, along with strong opinions of your own about how to bridge the gap between what AI can do today and how established companies get work done

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the team

Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building toward a fundamentally different kind of GRC: one that directs Claude, with the right humans in the loop, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits.

Within Security GRC, Audit & Assurance runs the integrated audit across our frameworks and maintains the Common Control Framework the program hangs off. This role sits in Audit & Assurance and helps run that integrated audit program, plan the audits we add next, and assess the frameworks and scope changes we are considering.

About the role

You'll help run Anthropic's unified audit program: quarterly audits across SOC 2, HIPAA and the ISO 27000 family including ISO 42001, plus the rest of our certifications, working with our audit firms, our GRC Partners, and control owners across the company. You'll plan new audits as we expand to new frameworks, platforms and regions, and run the gap assessments that tell us what each expansion takes before we commit to it.

You'll help build the audit operating model and runbook, and drive automation in the program so evidence is collected once and reused across frameworks, requests reach control owners once, and each audit cycle takes less effort than the last. Building with Claude is a normal part of the job, with you deciding where human judgment stays in the loop.

This is an individual contributor role for someone with program management experience who writes clearly, stays calm under deadlines, and likes making a busy program simpler.

Key responsibilities

- Run the audit program as a program: one integrated plan and calendar across audits and expansions, with milestones, dependencies, risks and decisions tracked, and regular status to GRC leadership and stakeholders

- Plan and run the quarterly audits, from scoping through report and findings closeout

- Run audit readiness ahead of each fieldwork window: control owner prep, evidence pre-checks and walkthrough dry runs

- Scope each audit's boundary with Product and Engineering: which products and deployment paths are in scope, and flag when a launch or new platform changes it

- Help build the audit operating model and runbook for a unified audit program, and keep both current as the program grows

- Drive automation in the program: evidence collected from source systems, request tracking and audit reporting, with evidence and walkthroughs reused across frameworks

- Coordinate audits across frameworks and firms so audit windows line up and control owners are asked for the same evidence once, and drive new ways of automated evidence generation and collection with GRC Engineering

- Plan new audits and audit expansions as we commit to them

- Run framework and scope expansion evaluations and gap assessments, with a recommendation and an effort estimate leadership can act on

- Manage day-to-day auditor relationships, and report audit status, findings and program metrics to GRC leadership

- Several years of program management: running multi-workstream programs with a plan, milestones, dependencies, risk tracking and status reporting to leadership

- Several years running external security audits (SOC 2 and ISO 27001 at minimum), on the company side or at an audit firm, including seasons with several frameworks at once

- Working knowledge of SOC 2, the ISO 27000 family, ISO 42001 and HIPAA, and where their requirements overlap

- Experience leading a gap assessment for a new framework or scope change and presenting the result to leadership

- Experience building or improving an audit process: calendars, request tracking, runbooks, roles and responsibilities

- Clear writing and calm coordination under deadline pressure

- Ability to get control owners to deliver on time without authority over them

- Audit firm experience (Big 4 or a SOC 2 or ISO certification body), especially as a senior or manager on technology clients

- Experience adding new frameworks such as PCI DSS, ISO 27701 or 27018, CSA STAR, or international schemes (for example IRAP, ISMAP or C5)

- Have automated evidence collection or audit reporting, or use Claude or other LLMs day to day to plan, track and report program work

- Experience with a GRC platform or building lightweight internal tooling

- Have done everything on this list. The combination is running a global audit calendar well, plus the instinct to make it simpler each cycle

- Hold every certification. CISA, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor or similar are welcome but not required

- Have prior AI industry experience

postings.location: Remote-Friendly (Travel Required) | San Francisco, CA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. You'll be the engineer who owns autonomous systems across that footprint as one security domain, from both sides: drones, ground robots and automated vehicles for patrol, inspection and moving hardware, including the security of that automation inside secure areas, and the detection systems that tell us what is flying over or operating near a site uninvited.

You set the approach, select and integrate the platforms and sensors, write the requirements vendors build to, and run what you ship, from the operating model where operators assign missions and machines carry them out to the playbook that turns a detection into an identified track and a well-evidenced handoff to whoever holds authority over the airspace. Interdiction is not part of this role. The goal is security that runs itself: coverage, fleet health and evidence verified continuously, with tools and AI agents doing the routine triage. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well.

You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including its physical security systems engineers and the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's data center operations and legal teams, and directly with site operators, equipment vendors and aviation and public safety authorities. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure.

Key responsibilities

- 

Autonomous security and inspection systems: own the drones, ground robots and other autonomous platforms for perimeter patrol, incident response and infrastructure inspection: platform selection, operating model, operator qualification, maintenance, and the data path from machine to analyst

- 

Tools, automation and AI agents: build the integrations that carry detections, tracks, telemetry and fleet health into the team's security monitoring platform, and the tools and agents that triage detections, check fleet health and assemble evidence. When a review keeps costing people time, you build the tool or agent that retires it

- 

Detection of uncrewed systems: engineer the sensing that tells us what is flying over or operating near a site, what it is and who needs to know: sensor selection and evaluation against live targets, per-site coverage, classification and false-alarm handling, and the playbook from first detection to handoff, with evidence retained

- 

Security of site automation: engineer the controls on automated vehicles, robots and similar machines that move hardware or work inside secure areas: identity and access, network isolation, what they may record and where it goes, fail-secure behavior, their place in chain of custody, and acceptance before they enter a site

- 

Regulatory and site constraints: establish what we may sense, fly, drive, record and retain at each site, partner-operated sites included, under the aviation, spectrum, privacy and safety rules that apply there, with the waivers and approvals that extend it and coordination with local authorities set up before it is needed

- 

Health monitoring: define and test heartbeats, loss-of-coverage and lost-link alarms and fail-secure behavior, so a silent sensor or machine shows as a fault, not a quiet day

- 

Vendor requirements and acceptance: write the requirements, evaluate against live flights and runs, and hold vendors to what they ship

Minimum qualifications

- 

Have engineered autonomous or sensing systems in the field (drones, ground robots, automated vehicles, or RF, radar or optical detection sensors): selected, integrated or secured them for an operation other people relied on, and verified what they actually do against real targets or runs rather than a datasheet

- 

Have integrated systems you did not build (vendor APIs, SDKs, appliances, machine and sensor telemetry) into a platform that outlives any one of them

- 

Read and review code, design the data systems behind security tooling, and build automation (often with AI coding agents) using Git and code review

- 

Have done this work hands-on for data centers, critical infrastructure or a large hardware fleet

- 

Have designed inside a regulatory or safety constraint (aviation, spectrum, privacy, machine safety or similar) and can show the decision it drove

- 

Own a domain end to end: set the approach, carry it through with vendors, site operators, partners and authorities, and run it as something people depend on every day

Preferred qualifications

- 

Remote pilot certification (for example FAA Part 107) and experience flying beyond visual line of sight under a waiver or exemption

- 

Experience with counter-drone (counter-UAS) detection, airspace surveillance or air traffic data systems

- 

Experience running a robot, drone or automated-vehicle fleet in an industrial, logistics or data center setting: fleet management, mission planning, safety cases

- 

Experience securing embedded, operational technology or robotic systems: device identity, network segmentation, update control, logging

- 

Experience with physical security operations at large sites, with law enforcement or aviation authorities, or at sites you did not fully control: cloud, colocation or GPU cloud operators

- 

Have built AI agents or automation that replaced recurring manual work

About Anthropic

About the role

We launch new products, models and pricing often, and each launch has to work in our systems on day one. A seller needs to be able to quote it, Deal Desk needs to be able to approve it, billing needs to charge for it correctly, and Finance needs to report on it. This role owns how a launch gets into our quote-to-cash systems, from the first pricing conversation to the first invoice.

We are looking for someone who treats every launch as a change across many systems. You will join launch planning early, work out what has to change across catalog, quoting, contracts, billing, tax and reporting, and get all of it ready before the launch date. You will build a good part of the Salesforce work yourself and partner with our Salesforce developers and Billing Engineering on the rest. You will be the named owner of the NPI process for systems, and the person Product, Pricing and Finance call when they want to know what it takes to launch something.

We are an AI-first systems team. You will use Claude as a normal part of how you design, build, test and document, and you will look for ways to make launches faster and more repeatable with AI.

- 

Own the systems side of new product and pricing launches, from the first pricing discussion through launch day and the first billing cycle

- 

Turn a pricing and packaging decision into concrete system changes: SKUs, price books, bundles, discount and approval rules, contract terms, billing plans, tax codes and reporting

- 

Build and run a repeatable NPI playbook: intake, a readiness checklist, sign-offs, a launch calendar and a post-launch review

Join launch planning early with Product and Pricing. Push back on pricing ideas that cannot be quoted, billed or reported cleanly, and offer options that can

Check every launch after it goes live: do quotes, orders, invoices and Finance reports match? Add the control or reconciliation that catches the gaps

Build and ship declarative solutions yourself where that is the right call, and write specs clear enough that developers can build the rest without several rounds of questions

Use AI to shorten launch cycles, for example generating catalog changes from a pricing spec, checking launch readiness, and testing quote and billing scenarios

postings.location: Remote-Friendly, United States
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

As a Capacity Deployment Lead within Anthropic's Data Center Operations (DCO) organization, you will support and scale how we bring new compute capacity online across a growing fleet of partner-operated data centers. Deployment runs from construction kickoff to ready for service (RFS). You are engaged during planning and construction, and on-site and hands-on from EFA through infrastructure delivery and receiving, integration QA, power-on and network turn-up, burn-in and validation, and acceptance. You work with hardware vendors and operations partners for completion of each CU (capacity unit) with a structured handover into production operations and the maintenance program. The scope is compute: accelerator systems, racks, and the infrastructure around them - at the sites in service today and the ones coming online behind them.

This is a program and execution role. You will work with the Global Capacity Delivery Program Lead and the broader Data Center Operations organization, to extend its coverage across more sites and platforms as the fleet grows. Expect 50%+ travel: you get eyes on via boots-on-the-ground for each site in preparation for and during delivery, deployment, QA, and close-out, and your authority comes from being there. Working with vendors and partners, you set direction, priorities, and standards for execution, and you prove results with Anthropic-owned data rather than self-reported status. What you learn at one site - what worked, what slipped, what should become standard - becomes the playbook for the next wave. If you have delivered data center hardware at scale, are passionate about HPC data centers, & enjoy working in complex, fast-paced environments, we welcome you to apply.

- 

Own deployment outcomes for your assigned sites and data-hall waves: CUs and hall ready-for-service dates met, with exceptions closed out, or risk called early enough for leadership to act.

Communicate deployment status, dependencies, constraints, and risk to engineering, capacity planning, the team that owns the overall site schedule, and leadership.

- 

Have 8+ years of experience in data center operations or hardware deployment as a manager, technical lead or related role, including accountability for delivery milestones.

- 

Can demonstrate a proven track record leading compute or network hardware deployments at a large scale across multiple sites or data-hall waves, from early floor access through ready for service.

Have managed vendors, OEMs, or contract workforces to measurable outcomes: milestones, quality gates, operational reviews, and corrective action.

-

- 

Have built or substantially improved operational processes.

- 

Can travel heavily and work on site for extended stretches, including during delivery surges and turn-up windows. 50% Travel expected.

Possess a bachelor's degree in relevant domain or equivalent practical experience.

Experience with GPU/accelerator or high-density liquid-cooled infrastructure, including bring-up of liquid-cooled racks.

- 

Experience standing up operations at a new site or data hall, from commissioning handoff through first deployment.

- 

Experience deploying more than one accelerator platform, or introducing a new hardware platform into an existing deployment program.

- 

Experience delivering deployment outcomes inside partner-operated or colocation sites where on-the-floor operations are staffed via third parties.

Familiarity with dense accelerator network cabling, optics, and high-speed interconnect at rack and pod scale.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

As a Channel Partner Manager for Korea, you will be responsible for building, managing, and scaling strategic partnerships with both System Integrators (SIs) and resellers to accelerate the adoption of our solutions in the Korean market. You will work at the intersection of cutting-edge technology and Korea's unique business ecosystem, helping partners integrate our products into their solution portfolios and joint go-to-market strategies.

As a Channel Partner Manager, you will focus on growing the partner Anthropic reseller and services business in Korea and achieving quarterly revenue and partner attach targets through new customers and upsells. You'll be the local owner of these partner relationships in Korea. Our partners will look to you for everything that makes the channel work day to day from initial onboarding to deal registration, enablement, billing and contracting questions, escalations. Our internal teams will look to you for what is happening in the market, how partners are driving new opportunities and growth within existing customers. You'll work closely with the local sales team and the central program team, co-selling on partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities and managing direct versus partner conflict as deals arise. Strong business creation skills are needed to identify joint value propositions and explore co-selling models. Much of the process for running the channel in Korea doesn't exist yet, and building it will be a large part of the job in the first year. While revenue contribution is the key metric, building scalable partner engagement and executing joint initiatives are crucial for consistent growth.

This is an early role in a new market for a program we expect to grow well beyond its first two countries. The habits you establish with our first partners in Korea will shape how the program works everywhere else.

Key responsibilities

- Own the day-to-day relationships with Anthropic's strategic resellers and system integrators in Korea, acting as their primary local point of contact, including billing, contracting and general queries

- Own deal registration and pipeline discipline with partners, making sure registrations are submitted and validated, conflicts are cleared, and named end-customer reporting is complete on every deal

- Forecast and report partner pipeline and performance against the quarterly revenue and partner attach targets, and own the Korea channel number with the central program team

- Negotiate resale agreements and commercial terms with partners alongside the central program team and Legal

- Co-sell with the local account team on partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities, and manage direct versus partner conflict as deals arise

- Develop and execute business plans with System Integrators and strategic resellers to drive mutual growth and revenue targets

- Build and maintain executive-level relationships within Korean partner organizations, navigating complex organizational structures and decision-making processes

- Support partner onboarding end to end, from diligence and agreement execution through readiness ahead of launch, including for partners who join the program after launch

- Coordinate partner certification and enablement with the central enablement lead, including Korean-language delivery and ongoing recertification

- Manage Anthropic's counterpart relationships with the cloud hyperscalers AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure in Korea, including the Marketplace private offer motion that reseller deals run through

- Run regular business reviews and QBRs with each partner against the joint plan

Anthropic’s Life Sciences team is working to make Claude a useful partner across biology and drug development, so that promising science can reach patients sooner. Genetic medicines are one area where we see real potential, particularly for diseases with few or no treatment options.

postings.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
postings.description:

About the role

Anthropic funds delivery partners to help customers adopt Claude, through assessments, workshops, proofs of concept, and full delivery engagements. Our partner request process is the front door for all of it: an account executive (AE) requests partner support, and the request is checked against program rules and matched to a partner.

Commercial is the program's highest-volume segment, and the one where a quick introduction and the right match matter most. Automation now drafts the first match and the introduction, and a vendor delivery team handles day-to-day follow-up and tracker updates. What's left is the work that needs a person sellers trust.

You'll be the one Activations contact for US Commercial sellers once a request is in, from submission to a partner on a signed statement of work (SOW). Partner Sales Managers (PSMs) attach the partner and own the opportunity, and at their volume they move on to the next deal. You'll own the follow-through: matching and re-matching, getting AE and customer introductions to happen, handling exception requests, and working the special cases that don't fit the standard path. Decision rights are clear: the program lead sets program rules, targets, and exception policy; you apply them on Commercial requests, decide what the rules already cover, and bring the rest with a recommendation.

We're looking for a partner seller or channel operator whom sellers and partners trust, who is comfortable owning a high-volume book, and who keeps following up until each request is closed. Success in this role comes down to three things: how quickly Commercial requests move from AE introduction to customer introduction and on to a signed SOW, whether sellers know exactly who to go to and get a straight answer, and whether exceptions are handled the same way every time.

Key responsibilities

- 

Serve as the single point of contact for the AE, the PSM, and the partner on every US Commercial request, from submission to confirmed SOW, so sellers deal with one person instead of several

- 

Answer "Where is my request?" with the current status, the blocker, and the next step with a date, and keep each request's record accurate enough that the answer is already written down

- 

Join the PSM pipeline and activation calls every week so requests don't slip between PSMs, and leave each call with an owner and a date on every open Commercial request discussed

- 

Own the request and its follow-through within clear boundaries: the PSM owns the opportunity, partner attach, and getting the SOW signed; the partner manager owns the partner relationship; and you hand over cleanly to Partner Success once the SOW is confirmed

- 

Confirm the first match that automation drafts from the partner bench, change it when it's wrong for the customer, and own the matching decision on Commercial requests; check that a partner has capacity before introductions go out, and spread work so no partner holds more open introductions than it can take

- 

Re-match quickly when a partner declines, stalls, or is turned down by the AE, record the reason, and make sure the request has an owner in between

- 

Review where Commercial matches are declined or lost, and turn repeat causes into changes to the matching rules

- 

Follow up on automatically drafted introductions that an AE hasn't approved, and resolve what the escalation rules send to you; step in when a partner's booking of the customer introduction stalls, and work with the AE or their manager to unblock it

- 

Run the regular review of aged Commercial requests, making sure each one has a recorded decision (introduction made, customer not ready, re-match, or close out) and a follow-up date

- 

Track every Commercial request from partner named to confirmed SOW, publish the baseline for that stage, and remove the blockers that sit with Anthropic

- 

Be the first stop for Commercial exception requests, including special order-form terms: resolve what the rules already cover, bring the rest to the program lead with the history, the blocker, and a recommended action, and log every exception consistently so approvals follow the agreed routing and can be audited later

- 

Work through cases the standard path doesn't fit, such as small and medium business (SMB), insurance, and other segment-specific use cases, and write down how each type is handled so the next one is faster

- 

Run tests of new funding programs, which start in Commercial, with sellers and partners, and report back what worked, what confused people, and what should change before a wider launch

- 

Teach Commercial AEs and their managers how to request a partner, how one-click introductions work, and what the response rules are, so requests arrive complete the first time; make sure PSMs and partner managers know the stage targets, who to contact once a request is in, and how escalations work

- 

Work with the activation systems and operations lead to turn repeat exceptions and repeat questions into rule changes or automation, so fewer requests need a person each quarter

- 

Use Claude to prepare for pipeline calls, draft follow-ups, and summarize the state of your book, and propose the next manual step worth automating

- 

Work US hours with a regular overlap window with the London-based program lead, and hand off cleanly so Commercial sellers have coverage across time zones

Minimum qualifications

- 

Experience in partner sales, channel, or partner operations in B2B technology

- 

Experience working with services partners or systems integrators: matching them to customer work, judging fit and capacity, and holding them to commitments

- 

Experience working alongside AEs and sales managers on live deals, and able to get a response from a busy AE while keeping the relationship strong

- 

Sound judgment on exceptions: knows the difference between a case the rules already cover and one that needs a decision, and makes a clear recommendation on the second kind

- 

Persistent, courteous follow-through with internal and external stakeholders, and doesn't let items slip past their deadline

- 

Clear, concise writing: short messages people act on, and escalations that give the facts, the ask, and a recommendation

- 

Comfortable with ambiguity and rules that change often: asks good questions, writes the answer down, and applies it consistently

- 

Works comfortably with records and reports in Salesforce

- 

Uses Claude or similar AI tools in day-to-day work

Preferred qualifications

- 

Experience as a Partner Sales Manager or in a closely related role

- 

Experience using Claude specifically in day-to-day work

- 

Experience with partner funding, market development funds (MDF), or co-sell programs

- 

Experience with order forms and SOW workflows

- 

Experience selling into SMB or insurance

You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.

Key responsibilities

- 

Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with parish presidents and councils, police juries, mayors and municipal officials, parish planning and zoning bodies, port, levee, and drainage districts, state economic development agencies, community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the Louisiana data center markets you cover

- 

Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations

- 

Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate

- 

Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media

- 

Monitor community sentiment and local political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement

- 

Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced

- 

Work with the Communications team to develop proactive, locally relevant messaging

- 

Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships

- 

Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use, including flood risk, storm resilience, and how large electricity needs are served by local utilities

- 

Build a community engagement playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

Minimum qualifications

- 

Experience in community affairs, public affairs, economic development, government relations, local or state government, or a closely related field

- 

Direct experience working for or engaging with parish and municipal governments and a broad set of community stakeholders on behalf of large infrastructure, construction, energy, or technology projects, with a working understanding of how local politics and community dynamics actually play out

- 

A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations

- 

The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings, including town halls, hearings, and press interviews

- 

Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to

- 

The ability to work independently, get up to speed quickly on complex policy issues, and manage multiple concurrent engagements across different markets without losing track of any of them

- 

Based in Louisiana or willing to relocate there, and prepared to travel regularly across the state

- 

7+ years of experience in community engagement specifically on data center, utility, energy, or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects, or in local government

- 

Familiarity with land use, zoning, and permitting processes at the parish and municipal level, including local review of industrial tax incentives

- 

Experience in communities with a long industrial, energy, or port presence, and an understanding of coastal, flood, and hurricane resilience concerns

- 

Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs

- 

Established relationships with economic development, workforce, or civic organizations in the markets this role covers

- 

Experience working with real estate, legal, communications, and policy teams at the same time

- 

Experience engaging with Tribal nations in Louisiana, including familiarity with consultation processes and Tribal sovereignty

- 

A genuine interest in the communities where you work, not just the projects you are managing

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.

We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Canada to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centres are sited, built, and operated. This role sits where community engagement, government relations and public affairs meet, and you may come from any of them. What matters is that you know how decisions get made in Alberta and can earn trust in a county council chamber, a minister's office or a community hall. Your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbour, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.

You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.

You will travel regularly within Alberta, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data centre markets. We will also consider applicants based in Ottawa who have established professional experience or relationships relevant to Alberta and can spend at least half their time in the province.

- 

Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with municipal governments, both elected and unelected, MLAs, provincial ministers and agencies, economic development organizations, community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the data centre markets you cover

- 

Engage respectfully and meaningfully with Indigenous communities, including First Nations, Metis Settlements, and Métis governments and organizations, building sustained relationships and supporting consultation and partnership efforts related to our projects

- 

Support projects through local decisions such as development permits and public hearings, working closely with our development partners and their community and Indigenous relations teams

- 

Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations

- 

Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate

- 

Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media

Work with Communications and Policy colleagues on public affairs in Alberta, including local media, advertising and trusted third-party voices

- 

Work with colleagues in Alberta to build a playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

- 

Experience in government relations, public affairs, political or government staff roles, community affairs, economic development, or a closely related field

- 

Direct experience working in or with Alberta's municipal or provincial governments, and a working understanding of how local and provincial politics and community dynamics actually play out

- 

A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations

- 

The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings, including town halls, hearings, and press interviews

Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to

Experience as political staff or in a senior government role in Alberta, at the municipal, provincial, or federal level

- 

Experience on a public affairs campaign that combined stakeholder outreach with earned or paid media

Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs

About the team

Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building toward a fundamentally different kind of GRC: one that directs Claude, with the right humans in the loop, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits.

Within Security GRC, Compliance & Audit Programs runs the integrated audit across our frameworks and maintains the Common Control Framework, the single set of controls that the whole program is built on. This role sits in Audit & Assurance and owns the framework and the assurance view across every control domain.

About the role

As part of the Security Audit & Controls team, you will own the CCF across every control domain, from access and change management to logging, encryption, and people controls: which controls we have, what each one says, how each maps to the frameworks and commitments we hold, and whether each one is actually working. You'll work with control owners and GRC Partners to draft and validate control descriptions and activities that describe reality rather than policy intent, build the monitoring that shows operating effectiveness continuously instead of once a year, and drive what monitoring finds to closure with control owners.

Building with Claude is a normal part of the job: drafting and mapping controls, testing evidence, and monitoring control health, with you deciding where human judgment stays in the loop.

This is an individual contributor role for someone who works well independently, writes clearly, and gets satisfaction from a control set that is accurate, tested, and trusted by auditors and engineers alike.

Key responsibilities

- Own the Common Control Framework: the canonical control set, its mappings to SOC 2, ISO 27001/42001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and customer commitments, and the change process for adding, retiring, or rewording controls

- Draft and validate control descriptions and control activities with control owners, so each control states who does what, how often, in which system, and what evidence proves it

- Design and run continuous monitoring of control efficacy: define the metrics and automated tests that show operating effectiveness, tune out false positives, surface failures to owners before an auditor does, and build the controls maturity model that shows where each control domain stands and what it takes to move up a level

- Verify remediation and carry it into steady state: GRC Partners lead remediation in their domains and control owners implement the fixes. This role advises on control design and implementation, confirms fixes against what the auditor actually asked for, and keeps one source of truth for control and finding status. Once a fix holds, it works with the partner to standardize the evidence pull and, where appropriate, automate it or build continuous

- Map new frameworks and commitments onto the CCF as we commit to them, and support gap assessments when a new framework, certification, product, or entity comes into scope, using the CCF as the baseline and writing the requirements for each delta

- Evaluate evidence reliability, including the completeness and accuracy of system-generated reports and AI-generated evidence, and set the standard for what audit-ready evidence looks like here

- Build with Claude: automate control mapping, evidence testing, and monitoring, and verify machine-drafted control language before it becomes the record

Minimum qualifications

- Several years in IT audit, security compliance, or controls assurance, including hands-on ownership of a control framework or control library across more than one framework (for example SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, HIPAA)

- Experience writing control descriptions, control activities, and test procedures that other teams and external auditors relied on

- Experience with continuous controls monitoring or automated evidence collection, whether you built it, ran it, or audited it

- Have stood up continuous controls monitoring or automated evidence programs and can speak to coverage, false-positive rates, and what changed as a result

- Have defined or assessed controls for AI systems or agents operating in production, or for home-built internal systems

- Have provided requirements for a homegrown GRC platform and worked with the engineers who build it

- Have done everything on this list. The scarce combination this role exists for is framework ownership plus the judgment to tell whether a control actually works
