postings.location: Remote-Friendly (Travel Required) | San Francisco, CA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Corporate Network Engineering designs, builds, and operates the networks in Anthropic's offices around the world: campus switching, Wi-Fi, and edge. We think a good office network is no more complicated than its requirements demand, fast and reliable enough that users never think about it, secure by default, and tolerant of failures to enable a lean team to operate a global portfolio of offices.

Anthropic is growing quickly, and our team is small and runs with high autonomy, so we care a great deal about how the work gets done: configuration kept in version control and shipped through review and staged rollouts, problems that happen more than once fixed at the source, and incidents closed only once the cause is fixed. We use Claude heavily in this work and expect you to as well.

We're hiring an experienced network engineer who works this way already: someone who has designed, built, and operated campus networks at scale, wired and wireless, and has also built the code and tooling to run them. As a network engineer here you'll work across all of it: network design and standards, new office buildouts, infrastructure as code, monitoring and incident response, and network security, where Corporate Security and Detection & Response are close partners. This is a hands-on individual contributor role.

Responsibilities

- Design, build, and operate campus networks for offices of every size: switching, Wi-Fi, edge, carrier, and out-of-band connectivity

- Contribute to the technical design standards 

- Build and maintain network infrastructure as code (source of truth, generated configuration, review, CI, staged rollout), and automate recurring manual work away

- Build monitoring and alerting that catches network problems early, respond to network events, and run incidents through to a fix for the cause

- Help establish the team's engineering practices, including change management, incident response, and post-incident review

- Partner with Corporate Security, Detection & Response, and Endpoint on network authentication, segmentation, and the network as a detection source

- Deliver the network for new offices end to end, from landlord and contractor requirements through carriers, cabling, staging, and cutover, alongside Buildouts, Workplace, and integrators

- Share the team's on-call rotation and travel to sites for buildouts, cutovers, and incidents (up to 25%)

You may be a good fit if you

- Have 8+ years designing, building, and operating enterprise campus networks, wired and wireless, for corporate offices across many sites

- Have deployed and operated Wi-Fi at scale that users never had to think about, including high-density spaces, and can trace a user complaint to its cause

- Treat network configuration as code, have written a substantial part of the pipeline that ships it, and have operated a network from it

- Write code well (Python or similar), build automation and tooling as a normal part of the job, and make a habit of automating yourself out of work

- Have built monitoring for a network, carried the pager for it, run incidents through to the fix, and helped a team adopt change management and post-incident review as a peer

- Have delivered the network for new offices end to end, with real estate, construction, carriers, and integrators

- Prefer the simplest design that meets the requirement, know what you gave up to get it, and write it down clearly enough for others to build from

- Hold a high bar for security, and have designed or deployed 802.1X/EAP-TLS and segmentation in partnership with a security team

- Already use AI tools as a core part of how you work, and know which work to hand to a model and which to keep

Strong candidates may also

- Have served as incident commander for incidents that spanned several teams, or built a team's on-call and incident process

- Have migrated a network between platforms or vendors across live sites

- Have designed segmentation for devices that cannot run an agent, such as AV, IoT, and physical security systems

Technical skills

- Campus switching and high-density Wi-Fi: L2/L3 design, Wi-Fi design for dense spaces, 6 GHz, roaming

- Access control and edge: 802.1X/EAP-TLS, RADIUS, segmentation, firewalls, multi-carrier BGP, out-of-band access

- Automation: Python, Ansible or Nornir, Terraform, vendor APIs, GitOps and CI

- Observability: streaming telemetry, flow and log pipelines, alerting

- Buildout infrastructure: MDF/IDF design, structured cabling, power and cooling, carrier diversity

- Any vendor: Arista, Cisco, Juniper, Aruba, Palo Alto, Fortinet, or equivalent

About the role

As a Customer Success Manager on Anthropic's Public Sector team, you will be the post-sales trusted advisor helping national security customers realize the value of Claude and turn their investment into mission impact. You'll combine your customer success expertise with technical fluency to drive adoption of Claude Code, the Claude API, and Claude for Government (C4G) on classified infrastructure delivered through a cleared cloud provider, while maintaining our high standards for safety, security, and discretion.

Working closely with our Sales, Applied AI, Product, Engineering, and Policy teams, you'll guide customers from deployment through enablement, model migration, renewal, and expansion. Your understanding of their mission, how they accredit and govern capabilities on classified fabrics, and how they evidence value to oversight will help them deliver decision advantage.

Drawing on both your national security expertise and technical knowledge, you'll serve as a strategic advisor throughout their journey with us—helping them navigate constraints that don't exist in commercial or federal civilian deployments: classified-fabric accreditation, fixed compute capacity, compartmentation, limited telemetry, and need-to-know discipline. Much of this work happens onsite, in the customer's spaces, on their systems. 

Your role focuses on driving consumption and adoption of Claude across mission workloads, standing up enablement and change management suited to a cleared, mission-driven workforce, identifying and hardening the workloads that matter most to the mission, and demonstrating value in unclassified terms that can leave the building and support renewal and expansion.

- Partner with the account executive and Applied AI architect to deeply understand the customer's mission requirements and translate them into an account and success plan, ensuring alignment between mission objectives, the customer's investment, and technical implementation

postings.title: Data Center Electrical Engineer – Design
postings.location: Remote-Friendly, United States
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for delivering that physical infrastructure — partnering with build partners, equipment manufacturers, and utilities to stand up facilities that can reliably power some of the largest accelerator clusters in the industry.

As a Data Center Electrical Engineer – Design, you'll own the electrical architecture of our facilities from the utility service entrance through to the rack — substation interface, medium- and high-voltage distribution, on-site generation and storage integration, UPS, switchgear, busway, and rack power. You'll develop and maintain the basis of design, reference architectures, and technical specifications that our build partners and A/E firms design against, and you'll be the point of technical authority when their drawings and calculations come back for review. You'll run the engineering studies — short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, load flow, and power quality — and you'll keep the architecture ahead of rapidly increasing rack densities and the unique load characteristics of large-scale ML training.

A central part of this role is speed-to-capacity through prefabrication: you'll shape Anthropic's offsite-manufactured electrical strategy — modular skids, e-houses, and prefabricated power assemblies — and drive its standardization across sites. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team, with our hardware and compute teams to translate accelerator requirements into electrical design criteria, and with supply chain to qualify and diversify regional equipment vendors. Expect roughly 10–25% travel for design reviews, partner and vendor meetings, factory witness testing, and site visits to support commissioning and startup.

Responsibilities

Electrical design & engineering

- 

Lead the electrical design of critical data center infrastructure across the US portfolio, including the utility interface and substation, site medium- and high-voltage distribution, generators, UPS, switchgear, transformers, busway, and grounding

- 

Develop and maintain Anthropic's electrical basis of design, reference architectures, and technical specifications for critical power distribution — covering switchgear, UPS systems, PDUs, busway, and rack power delivery — producing designs that meet our reliability and maintainability requirements while staying within budgetary targets

- 

Perform and validate engineering studies — including short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, load flow, and power quality analysis — and use the findings to steer topology, redundancy, equipment-selection, and protection-setting decisions

- 

Design and plan data center hall power distribution layouts for newly allocated spaces in coordination with the telecom, mechanical and cooling design

Prefabrication & modular delivery

- 

Drive Anthropic's prefabricated and modular electrical strategy — developing modular skids, e-houses, and prefabricated power assemblies, and partnering with external engineering and manufacturing teams on a productization roadmap that accelerates deployment and reduces onsite labor

- 

Design for offsite manufacture and onsite assembly: define the interfaces between prefabricated components and site-built work, and the electrical interfaces and switchover points for temporary-to-permanent power sequencing

- 

Drive standardization of modular electrical designs across sites to compress deployment timelines while preserving flexibility for site-specific constraints and evolving hardware generations

Partner, vendor & utility coordination

- 

Work with regional vendors and manufacturers to specify and qualify major electrical equipment, and partner with supply chain to build a diversified vendor base that mitigates lead-time and single-source risk

- 

Work with utilities and interconnection/transmission operators (e.g., ISOs/RTOs) to define site utility service and interconnection requirements, and with local authorities having jurisdiction to ensure designs comply with the National Electrical Code (NFPA 70/NEC), NFPA, IEEE, UL/ANSI, and local requirements

- 

Work with Anthropic's hardware and compute teams to translate accelerator power, density, and power-quality requirements into electrical design criteria, and keep the reference architecture aligned with upcoming hardware generations

- 

Present findings and design positions to internal stakeholders, build partners, and operations teams through clear reports and presentations, and defend them under challenge

Design review & quality

- 

Review and approve electrical design packages, calculations, submittals, and shop drawings from build partners and MEP consultants; track clarifications, deviations, and exceptions against the basis of design, and hold the line on capacity, reliability, maintainability, and safety requirements

- 

Perform technical due diligence and design reviews on data center developer and partner projects — evaluating their electrical single-lines, equipment selections, studies, and specifications against Anthropic's reliability, maintainability, and capacity requirements

- 

Define project electrical scope and serve as the design authority on RFIs and field changes that affect design intent during procurement and construction

- 

Support factory acceptance testing, commissioning, and startup — reviewing test procedures and results against design intent, participating on site for key milestones, and closing as-built changes back into the reference design

-

postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. Anthropic’s Data Center team is responsible for delivering that physical infrastructure — partnering with build partners, equipment manufacturers, and vendors to stand up facilities that can reliably cool some of the largest accelerator clusters in the industry.

As a Senior Data Center Mechanical Engineer based in the United States, you’ll lead the design direction and technical oversight of building mechanical systems — cooling, chilled-water distribution, liquid cooling, plumbing, and fire protection — across our rapidly expanding U.S. portfolio. This is a senior individual contributor role focused on driving and reviewing mechanical design from concept through detailed design and construction documentation produced by external engineering firms and development partners, ensuring every facility meets Anthropic’s standards for reliability, efficiency, and scalability. You’ll own the mechanical design direction from Basis of Design through construction and commissioning, serving as the primary technical interface between Anthropic’s internal teams and our external engineering and development partners.

A central part of this role is speed-to-capacity through prefabrication and modular construction — modular cooling skids, prefabricated piping assemblies, and design for offsite manufacture that compress schedules and reduce onsite labor. You’ll bring deep familiarity with U.S. mechanical, plumbing, and fire codes and the local regulatory environment, and ensure the cooling architecture keeps pace with rapidly increasing rack densities and the shift toward direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Strong candidates will bring deep mission-critical mechanical design experience and the judgment to make sound trade-offs when the standard playbook doesn’t apply.

Responsibilities

Design direction & review

- 

Drive mechanical design concepts for data center cooling plants, chilled-water distribution, liquid cooling (direct-to-chip and CDUs), plumbing, and fire protection systems.

- 

Review and direct design drawings, specifications, and construction documentation produced by external engineering firms, ensuring alignment with Anthropic’s Basis of Design and owner requirements.

- 

Evaluate design submittals, shop drawings, and equipment selections; respond to RFIs with clear technical direction.

- 

Identify design conflicts and drive resolution across mechanical, electrical, and controls disciplines.

- 

Maintain and evolve Anthropic’s internal mechanical design standards and reference configurations.

Prefabrication & modular delivery

- 

Drive Anthropic’s prefabricated and modular mechanical strategy — modular cooling skids, prefabricated piping and pump assemblies, and design for offsite manufacture and onsite assembly — to accelerate deployment and reduce onsite labor.

- 

Drive standardization of modular mechanical designs across sites while preserving flexibility for site-specific constraints and evolving hardware generations.

External partner & vendor coordination

- 

Serve as the primary mechanical engineering point of contact for external developers, design engineers, and construction partners across the U.S. portfolio.

- 

Develop scopes of work, equipment specifications, and bid packages for mechanical infrastructure.

- 

Perform technical due diligence on third-party and colocation facilities, evaluating mechanical designs against program requirements and redundancy targets.

- 

Coordinate with equipment vendors and manufacturers on cooling system procurement, including chillers, CDUs, pumps, and piping assemblies, and partner with supply chain to mitigate lead-time and single-source risk.

Construction & commissioning

- 

Monitor mechanical system installation for compliance with design intent, applicable U.S. codes and standards, and industry best practice.

- 

Conduct site visits to review progress, resolve field issues, and validate construction quality; travel to sites across the region as needed.

- 

Support testing and commissioning of mechanical systems; analyze data and troubleshoot issues against design intent.

You may be a good fit if you

- 

Have 10+ years of experience designing building mechanical systems for data centers or mission-critical facilities, across the project lifecycle from concept design through construction, commissioning, and handover.

- 

Have deep familiarity with U.S. mechanical, plumbing, and fire codes and standards — including the International Mechanical Code (IMC), International Plumbing Code (IPC), International Energy Conservation Code (IECC), International Building Code (IBC), NFPA 13 (automatic sprinkler systems), ASME B31 piping codes, and applicable state and local amendments, alongside ASHRAE guidance (incl. TC 9.9).

- 

Have strong knowledge of chilled-water systems, air-cooled cooling plants, liquid cooling (direct-to-chip and CDUs), and redundant piping configurations.

- 

Have hands-on experience with prefabricated and modular mechanical infrastructure — modular cooling skids, prefabricated piping assemblies, and design for offsite manufacture.

- 

Have experience driving and reviewing mechanical design work produced by external engineering consultants, and are proficient reading and marking up construction drawings, P&IDs, and single-line diagrams.

- 

Hold a bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering; a Professional Engineer (PE) license (or eligibility) is valued but not required.

- 

Communicate clearly and can drive technical decisions across internal teams and external partners, and are results-oriented with a bias toward practical solutions.

- 

Are able to travel up to ~30% to data center sites across the region.

Strong candidates may also have

- 

15+ years of experience designing building mechanical systems for data centers or mission-critical facilities.

- 

Direct project experience delivering data centers in multiple U.S. markets (e.g., Virginia, Ohio, Texas, Arizona, Oregon).

- 

Experience with thermal-hydraulic modeling software (AFT Fathom, Cadence 6SigmaET, ANSYS, or similar), CFD modeling, and energy analysis.

- 

Familiarity with controls/BAS systems and sequences of operation for cooling plants.

- 

Experience preparing SOWs, facility audits, and TCO analyses.

- 

A track record building modular prefabricated products in mechanical or electrical areas of the data center, and driving designs toward offsite manufacturing.

-

postings.location: Remote-Friendly, United States
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. The loads involved are large enough — and arrive fast enough — that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI).

As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio. That means the on-site generation fleet — reciprocating engine gensets, gas turbines, fuel cells — and the battery energy storage systems that buffer load steps and provide ride-through. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection. You'll also own our temporary- and bridging-generation strategies — the plans that let a site energize and start serving load before permanent utility service is available, and transition cleanly once it is.

This is a deeply cross-functional role. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team on where and how generation and storage tie into the site electrical distribution, controls, and SCADA, and with our hardware and compute teams to understand the load characteristics you're designing against. You'll be Anthropic's technical counterpart to on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, utilities, and ISOs/RTOs. Expect roughly 20–35% travel for design reviews, factory witness testing, and site startup.

Responsibilities

On-site generation engineering

- 

Own Anthropic's behind-the-meter generation architecture across the portfolio — prime-mover selection and sizing (reciprocating engines, gas turbines, fuel cells), paralleling topology, redundancy, fuel systems, and emissions controls — and maintain the generation basis of design and technical specifications that build partners and generation providers design against

- 

Set the day-one vs. day-N plant sizing and expansion strategy — what the plant needs on day one so it can be expanded or augmented later, and how to add units, storage, or a grid tie to a system already running

- 

Characterize the data center load for external generation partners — step changes, ramps, oscillation, fault behavior, and non-IT load — so providers can size and tune their plant against the real duty

- 

Model generation response against the load profile of large-scale ML training — step-load acceptance, block loading, transient frequency and voltage response, load rejection — and set the acceptance criteria (e.g., per ISO 8528-5) that generation packages are tested against

- 

Develop temporary- and bridging-generation strategies that deliver early site energization ahead of permanent utility service, including the sequencing, protection, and controls changes needed to transition from temporary to permanent power without stranding equipment or capacity

- 

Ensure generation designs meet NFPA 37, NFPA 110 where the plant provides emergency or legally required standby power, fuel-gas and fuel-storage codes (e.g., NFPA 54, NFPA 30), and applicable emissions requirements, and coordinate with environmental and permitting counterparts on the technical inputs to air permits

Energy storage & microgrid architecture

- 

Size and specify battery energy storage systems for ride-through, step-load buffering, and power-quality support — including cell chemistry and enclosure selection, inverter selection (grid-forming vs. grid-following), UL 9540 listing, UL 9540A large-scale fire test data, and NFPA 855 installation requirements — and own the thermal and fire-protection interfaces

- 

Define the site microgrid topology and operating modes — grid-parallel, islanded, and black-start — and the transition logic between them, including load-shedding schemes, resynchronization criteria, and the conditions under which the site separates from and reconnects to the utility

- 

Specify the functional requirements for the microgrid controller — generation dispatch, set-point coordination across rotating and inverter-based sources, mode management — and drive its implementation, testing, and integration into site SCADA and the electrical power monitoring system (EPMS)

- 

Help define the protection and control requirements for generation and storage sources so that interconnection protection, anti-islanding, and source-transfer schemes are consistent from the generator terminals through the point of interconnection

Grid interconnection & power quality

- 

Lead the technical side of utility interconnection for sites with on-site generation or storage — interconnection applications, studies, and agreements, ISO/RTO processes, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and interconnection protection

- 

Own power quality at the point of interconnection — flicker per IEEE 1453, harmonics per IEEE 519, voltage regulation, reactive-power and power-factor requirements — and design the generation, storage, and filtering mitigations needed to keep the site within its interconnection limits under real training-load behavior

- 

Run or critically review the power-system studies that support interconnection and microgrid design — load flow, short-circuit contribution from rotating and inverter-based sources, transient stability, motor-starting and step-load studies, and electromagnetic-transient studies where inverter controls matter

Vendor diligence & delivery

- 

Lead technical due diligence on on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, and microgrid-controller vendors — evaluating equipment and controls on engineering merit, stress-testing performance and availability guarantees, and reviewing proposed architectures against Anthropic's basis of design

- 

Define the technical performance terms in energy-services agreements with on-site generation providers — availability, power quality, ramp, and ride-through, each with a definition, meter, test protocol, and acceptance criteria — working with energy commercial and legal counterparts

- 

Review and disposition design packages, submittals, shop drawings, and deviation requests from generation providers and their EPCs, and hold partners to Anthropic's reliability and maintainability requirements

- 

Support commissioning of generation, storage, and microgrid systems — witnessing factory and site acceptance tests, defining and observing integrated systems tests (islanding, resynchronization, black-start, load-step), and resolving field issues against design intent

- 

Manage concurrent generation and microgrid scopes across multiple sites, and contribute to the continuous improvement of Anthropic's generation and interconnection design standards as the portfolio and the technology both evolve

You may be a good fit if you

- 

Have 10+ years of engineering experience in power generation, microgrids, battery energy storage, or utility interconnection, with substantial time spent on on-site or distributed generation for mission-critical, data center, or large industrial loads, and deep hands-on delivery experience in at least one of these areas (generation, storage, microgrids, or interconnection)

- 

Have deep hands-on experience with one or more generation technologies — reciprocating engine gensets (diesel and natural gas), gas turbines, or fuel cells — including sizing, paralleling, fuel systems, and emissions controls

- 

Understand the thermal generation asset classes — reciprocating engines across the size range (sub-MW through 10–20 MW units), small- and medium-frame combustion turbines, and combined cycles — and how each responds to fast load changes and holds stable islanded operation

- 

Understand battery energy storage sizing for a defined duty (ride-through, load-step buffering, peak shaving), inverter selection (grid-forming vs. grid-following), UL 9540 listing, UL 9540A test data, and NFPA 855 installation requirements

- 

Understand microgrid architecture end to end — islanding detection and transition, resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch

- 

Are fluent in interconnection standards and processes — IEEE 1547, IEEE 2800, utility interconnection requirements, and ISO/RTO study and queue processes

- 

Are comfortable running or critically reviewing power-system studies — load flow, short-circuit, transient stability, and power quality — in tools such as ETAP, SKM, PSS®E, PSCAD, or EasyPower

- 

Hold a bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, or a closely related field, or have equivalent practical experience; Professional Engineer (PE) licensure is valued but not required

- 

Have worked directly with generation OEMs, BESS integrators, generation-as-a-service providers, or utilities, and can evaluate equipment and proposals on technical merit rather than datasheet claims

- 

Communicate clearly with technical peers, utilities, regulators, and non-specialist stakeholders, and are results-oriented with a bias toward practical solutions and a willingness to pick up work outside your core remit when the team needs it

Strong candidates may also have

- 

Designed or delivered battery energy storage systems at MW scale

- 

Specified or commissioned a microgrid controller for a site that can island and resynchronize

- 

Taken at least one large load or generation interconnection from application through agreement

- 

HV/MV substation design experience — main one-line development, equipment specification, grounding, and layout — since on-site generation and storage tie in at the substation and the two scopes are tightly coupled

- 

A protection-engineering background covering generation and interconnection protection — relay selection and settings, anti-islanding schemes, and coordination between on-site sources and utility protection

- 

Experience integrating renewable generation (solar PV, wind) with storage into hybrid behind-the-meter plants

- 

Experience on the technical side of air permitting for stationary generation (e.g., Title V, NSR/PSD, or state equivalents) and emissions-control equipment selection

- 

Electromagnetic-transient (EMT) modeling experience in PSCAD or EMTP for inverter-based resource and microgrid-transition studies

- 

Direct experience with data center, hyperscaler, or other large-campus microgrids, or at a generation provider, BESS integrator, or developer serving those customers

- 

A track record of authoring generation or interconnection reference designs or standards that were adopted across multiple sites or by external partners

postings.title: DevOps / AgentOps Engineer, GTM Systems
postings.location: San Francisco, CA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Go To Market ("GTM") Systems builds and runs the platform that Sales and contracting operate on, a production Salesforce org plus a growing portfolio of custom internal applications and agents. These systems process revenue-impacting transactions, guide critical business processes, and produce data the rest of the company runs on. Today the path from request, development, test, and pull request to production push is manual and slows the team down rather than speeding it up.

We are hiring a DevOps / AgentOps engineer to build and run that path. You will stand up and maintain an AI-first CI/CD pipeline covering both Salesforce and custom application code. This release pipeline will support three modes: fully agentic, human-in-the-loop, and AI-assisted. Anthropic is an unusual place to do this. Our own frontier models are part of the toolkit and the question we want you to answer is what a delivery system looks like when you design it for agents and humans working side by side rather than retrofitting agents into a pipeline built for humans alone.

You will work closely with a team of business systems analysts, software engineers, and integration engineers to develop the solution to accelerate their everyday work. The pipeline you build is the one path to production for a system under audit, so the guardrails, approvals, and audit trail are part of the product, not an afterthought.

Key responsibilities

- Design, build, and operate the CI/CD pipeline for a production Salesforce org and a portfolio of custom internal applications, from branching and validation through deploy and rollback

- Define how a change is classified and routed into an agentic, human-in-the-loop, or AI-assisted lane, what gates each lane passes through, and how a change escalates between lanes when validation fails or risk changes

- Build the agent operations layer: what agents are scoped to do in the pipeline, what tools and permissions they hold, how they are sandboxed differently for Salesforce and custom-app work, and what they are not trusted to do unsupervised

- Implement approval workflows that keep PR review and business sign-off as distinct gates, with clear rules for which changes need which, who is asked, and what evidence they see

- Own environment strategy, secrets handling, deploy observability, and kill-switch and rollback mechanics across all three lanes

- Produce the audit trail and evidence a SOX-scoped platform needs

- Measure and report on the pipeline itself: lead time, failure rate, share of work moving through each lane, and where humans are still doing work an agent should be doing

- Pair with engineers on the team as they move onto the pipeline, and turn what you learn from them into better defaults

Minimum qualifications

- Have built and run a CI/CD pipeline for a team, including the branching model, merge gating, and rollback path, and can explain the choices you made and what you would change

- Have hands-on experience with Salesforce deployment mechanics (metadata API, source-tracked development, org-to-org promotion) or a comparable enterprise platform

- Work fluently with AI coding tools and agentic workflows, and have opinions about which kinds of engineering work belong in the hands of an agent, which need a human review, and where the boundaries are

- Design for the failure case: you think about blast radius, sandboxing, permissions, and what happens when an automated change is wrong before you think about the happy path

- Are comfortable working across GitHub Actions or a comparable CI system, infrastructure as code, and the scripting needed to glue platforms together

- Write clear design documents and can defend a design to engineers, business approvers, and auditors in language each of them will accept

Preferred qualifications

- Have shipped agents or automation that operate inside a production system of record, and have dealt with what happens when they misbehave

- Have operated a platform under SOX or a similar audit regime and know what evidence a change-management control actually requires

- Have experience with Salesforce DevOps tooling (Gearset, Copado, sfdx-based pipelines) and know where those tools stop and custom work begins

- Have run a migration from ad hoc or manual deploys to a governed pipeline and can talk about how you kept a team shipping while you did it

- Have built approval or notification workflows in Slack or a comparable tool that people actually used

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the Role

We are looking for a SOX Director - Compute and Infrastructure to join our Internal Audit team at Anthropic. In this role, you will lead financial risk assessment and internal control design over compute and infrastructure. This is Anthropic's largest cost and one of the most complex areas of our financial reporting. You'll focus on cloud spend, usage-based costs, vendor commitments, accruals, and cost allocation, as we scale rapidly toward an IPO.

This is a unique opportunity to build SOX controls at an AI-first company, in a domain where few established playbooks exist. Compute is purchased under multi-year agreements with multiple providers, metered in third-party environments, accrued from internal telemetry, and increasingly provisioned and scheduled by automated systems and agents. You will help define how controls work in that environment for both business and IT environments, from reliance on service providers to full-population monitoring of high-volume usage data, while maintaining the rigor required for public company compliance.

As the SOX Director, Compute and Infrastructure, you will own scoping, control design, testing, remediation, and reporting for compute and infrastructure processes, partnering directly with Compute Accounting, Finance Analytics & BI, Infrastructure Engineering, Finance & Strategy, and Procurement to design scalable controls, oversee documentation, and support communication with external auditors. This role reports to the Head of Business Controls and plays a critical part in strengthening internal control maturity through pre-IPO readiness and beyond.

Key responsibilities

- Lead financial risk and internal control design for compute and infrastructure accounting, including cloud spend, usage-based costs, vendor commitments, credits, refunds, accruals, cost allocation, budgeting, and asset lifecycle management

- Develop and execute the SOX control plan and roadmap for compute and infrastructure, making defensible prioritization calls on what must be controlled now and what can follow

- Own scoping, risk assessment, walkthroughs, testing, remediation, and reporting activities for compute and infrastructure processes

- Build scalable, automated, and sustainable controls to support growth through pre-IPO and post-IPO readiness

- Pioneer the use of AI and automation to enhance control effectiveness, including full-population matching of usage to invoices, continuous monitoring, and anomaly detection

- Design, implement, and monitor controls over the completeness, accuracy, and cutoff of compute cost, including monthly accruals built from internal workload telemetry and the true-up to provider invoices

- Establish controls over multi-year provider agreements, including reserved capacity, minimum spend commitments, usage-based charges, signing credits, service-level credits, refunds, and billing corrections

- Design and test controls over the allocation of compute cost between cost of revenue and research and development, including workload tagging, shared clusters, and changes to tagging logic or allocation models

- Establish the investigation threshold and variance criteria used in the control design to ensure the precision needed to detect a material misstatement

- Design and test controls over infrastructure related control inclusive of development of an asset lifecycle management system

- Oversee control documentation and ensure audit-ready evidence is maintained for all compute and infrastructure processes, in compliance with US GAAP and SEC reporting requirements

- Own control requirements across high-volume financial data pipelines, partnering with Finance Analytics &BI, Finance & Strategy, and Accounting to validate completeness, accuracy, classification, general-ledger mapping, key reports, and monthly close governance

- Own the identification and control treatment of key reports and Information Produced by the Entity (IPE) used in compute accruals, allocation, and the close

- Partner with IT SOX and engineering teams on the IT general controls and automated controls that support compute data, including interface, ITAC’s, and change management over pipelines and models

- Embed control requirements into new systems, pipelines, and process changes at design time

- Lead the assessment of reliance on cloud providers that meter and bill compute, including review of SOC 1 reports, scope and period coverage, bridge letters, and exceptions or qualified opinions

- Define and monitor complementary user entity controls, and design alternative procedures where a provider report is missing, does not cover the relevant system or period, or includes exceptions

- Assess how the use of AI in Finance and in the close changes what controls need to cover, and update the control environment accordingly

- Partner with Compute Accounting, Finance Analytics & BI, Infrastructure Engineering, Procurement, and Finance & Strategy to implement scalable controls over compute and infrastructure

- Work with the Compute Controller and Chief Accounting Officer organizations to align control priorities with business objectives

- Train and enable process owners and control performers, many of whom are new to SOX, on control execution, evidence retention, and what audit-ready means

- Support management's assessment of internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR) and related disclosures

- Serve as the primary point of contact for external auditors on compute and infrastructure SOX matters

- Prepare the Company's formal positions on control design, provider reliance, and deficiency evaluation for compute and infrastructure

- Manage audit requests, coordinate testing schedules, and facilitate walkthroughs across compute and infrastructure processes

- Track and report on control status, testing results, and remediation to leadership

- Drive alignment with external auditors on testing approaches, reliance strategies, and deficiency evaluation and aggregation assessment

Minimum qualifications

- Have designed controls over cloud, compute, or infrastructure cost, or over a comparable high-volume, usage-based process, and understand control objectives, IPE, and sufficiency of audit evidence

- Have proven ability to establish or scale SOX controls at newly public or pre-IPO companies

- Possess deep understanding of compute accruals, vendor commitments, cost allocation, financial close, and US GAAP requirements

- Have experience evaluating service organization reports (SOC 1 and SOC 2) and complementary user entity controls

- Are comfortable working with large datasets and data pipelines, and partnering with data science and engineering teams

- Can structure ambiguous control problems and influence across stakeholders without direct authority

- Have strong project management, analytical, and communication skills

- Hold a Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, IT/Engineering

- Are passionate about building scalable processes that support organizational growth and Anthropic's mission to create safe AI

Preferred qualifications

- Have 12+ years of hands-on SOX, internal audit, or internal controls experience, preferably in both Big 4 and in-house roles at a fast-paced technology company

- CPA (or similar certification) and/ or CISA

- Familiarity with cloud provider billing and commitment structures (AWS, GCP, Azure)

- SQL and comfort working directly with usage, telemetry, and cost data to validate what the systems are telling you

- Experience with controls over cost of revenue, gross margin reporting, and allocation methodologies

- Interest in or experience applying AI/ML technologies to audit, compliance, or risk management processes

- Understanding of lease accounting (ASC 842) and other accounting standards relevant to infrastructure and capacity arrangements

- Experience working at a high-growth AI or technology company

- Familiarity with financial data governance, internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR), and SEC disclosure requirements

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

We are looking for a Director, Technical Revenue Accounting to join our Accounting Team. In this role, you will own the company’s most complex ASC 606 technical positions, lead the revenue accounting memo portfolio, and serve as the senior accounting decision-maker for new product revenue recognition treatments, non-standard deal structures, and partnership / marketplace go-to-market initiatives. You will partner directly with Deal Desk, Product, Legal, and Partnership leadership and set the technical revenue policy direction for the company! If you are looking for an opportunity to make a significant impact on the financial infrastructure of an innovative company, come join us in our mission to build cutting-edge, safe AI.

Key responsibilities

- Own the company’s ASC 606 technical accounting memo portfolio — authoring and reviewing position papers on the most complex and judgment-intensive revenue recognition scenarios, including the SSP study

- Lead the technical revenue assessment for all new product offerings (NPI) and programs, serving as the accounting decision-maker on performance obligation identification, SSP evaluation, and contract modification frameworks, and providing authoritative guidance to Product, Pricing, and GTM cross-functional teams

- Serve as the senior Revenue Accounting partner to Deal Desk, Sales, and Legal — structuring non-standard deal terms, and providing real-time revenue recognition guidance on the company’s largest and most strategic commercial arrangements

- Provide technical accounting guidance on partnership and marketplace arrangements for cloud third-party channels, including principal-vs-agent determinations, and revenue-share / co-sell economics

- Own key accounting processes such as SSP analysis and related allocations, contractual credit amortization, reseller/partner channel incentives and rebates, footnote disclosures etc. 

- Own the revenue contract review framework, including ASC 606 checklists, position papers, and escalation paths, ensuring revenue recognition compliance scales with deal volume

- Lead technical research initiatives on emerging revenue recognition issues and present recommendations to the Controller

- Translate complex technical accounting requirements into actionable business guidance for non-accounting stakeholders

- Review revenue-related month end close journal entries and flux analysis

- Drive process improvement and revenue system implementation projects, including scoping, design sign-off, and UAT ownership

Minimum qualifications

- Have a track record of authoring technical accounting memos on complex, judgment-intensive revenue arrangements

- Have strong knowledge of ASC 606 with experience in performance obligation analysis, standalone selling prices, contract modification accounting, considerations payable to a customer, principal versus agent analysis, material rights, and variable consideration treatment

- Ability to articulate complex accounting positions clearly, and proactively conduct technical accounting research to identify emerging revenue recognition challenges

- Have hands-on experience with revenue recognition tools (e.g., Workday Financial Management, Zuora RevPro)

- Have SQL proficiency for querying and analyzing large revenue and contract datasets

- Have proven ability to lead cross-functional workstreams across Deal Desk, Product, and Partnership teams and drive results

- Have a demonstrated ability to thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments

- Have 14+ years of progressive accounting experience, with extensive expertise in ASC 606 implementation and complex revenue recognition scenarios, including 4+ years in a technical revenue leadership or managerial role

- A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA required with demonstrated technical accounting expertise

- Big 4 technical accounting / national office background combined with industry experience

- Experience with technical accounting advisory work, including revenue recognition consulting or implementation experience

- Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller, or channel partnership revenue arrangements

- Experience working with consumption-based and subscription-based revenue models

- Knowledge of AI/ML, SaaS and technology sector revenue recognition complexities

About the role

Anthropic's legal team operates at the frontier of some of the most consequential legal and regulatory questions of our time — from landmark copyright matters to first-of-their-kind AI regulatory frameworks emerging across dozens of jurisdictions simultaneously. As we scale, the volume and complexity of our discovery and information governance obligations are growing rapidly.

We are looking for a Discovery Technical Operations Specialist to join our Litigation and Regulatory team and help build out Anthropic's discovery operations from the ground up, support active matters, and help drive information governance maturation. This is a unique opportunity to be a part of a critical function at one of the most closely watched companies in the world. You will work hand-in-hand with our discovery leads, litigation and regulatory counsel, outside counsel, discovery vendors, and cross-functional partners such as Security and IT to manage retention, preservation, collection, and production of electronically stored information (ESI) across active matters. Beyond matter-level support and programmatic development of discovery systems and processes, you will also help execute the development of Anthropic's broader information governance program, including data classification standards and defensible disposal practices that keep pace with a rapidly scaling AI company's evolving data landscape.

The right person for this role will be equal parts technical operator and operational project manager.

Key responsibilities

- 

Build and operate discovery operations across the full EDRM lifecycle (preservation, collection, processing, hosting, review, and production including for novel and AI-specific data types)

- 

Support the operational design and execution of the legal hold program including custodian identification workflows, hold issuance and tracking, periodic re-notification, custodian acknowledgments, and defensible release

- 

Support and improve the discovery technology stack including RelativityOne, in-place preservation and collection tooling across Slack, Google Workspace, and internal systems, and supporting analytics and review platforms including configuration, access controls, templates, and reusable workspaces

- 

Strong project management instincts and a track record of running multiple concurrent matters and programs under tight deadlines, with composure and precision

- 

Demonstrated ability to communicate technical discovery and operational concepts clearly to attorneys, executives, engineers, and non-technical stakeholders

Preferred qualifications

- 

6+ years of hands-on discovery experience across the full EDRM lifecycle

- 

Experience standing up discovery operations at a young and/or fast-scaling company, particularly in the context of new kinds of ESI

- 

Experience embedding with engineering or product teams to define discovery and information governance requirements, prioritize roadmap, and ship hold-capable and collection-capable features into core enterprise tools

- 

Hands-on integration of generative AI and agentic workflows (e.g., Claude, Claude Code, or similar) into operational discovery work project tracking, status reporting, internal documentation, custom tooling, and script maintenance

- 

Technical fluency working with engineering teams and modern infrastructure APIs, cloud (AWS, GCP), data pipelines, and version control and comfort writing, reading, or maintaining small scripts where useful

- 

Experience operating information governance programs at scale including retention scheduling, data classification, defensible disposition, and data mapping across heterogeneous enterprise data sources

- 

Experience with applying AI and automation to discovery operations, including generative AI for review, agentic automation, and operational tooling for hold tracking, reporting, and documentation

A collaborative, hands-on orientation, with integrity and genuine curiosity about building operational programs in a fast-moving environment

postings.title: Docs Lead, Platform
postings.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

As Platform Docs Lead at Anthropic, you will be the single-threaded owner of developer documentation for the Claude Platform. You'll own the information architecture, the content, and the overall experience of platform.claude.com/docs — from a developer's first quickstart to the reference page they keep open in a pinned tab.

This role sits on the DevX team and is closer to DevRel than to traditional technical writing. The job is taste, judgment, and end-to-end developer empathy in addition to strong writing skills: you'll be expected to build with the Claude API yourself, understand the product firsthand, and turn that understanding into documentation developers genuinely love.

You'll also own documentation written for AI agents and contribute to the skill that teaches Claude how to help developers use the Claude API. Writing for an LLM reader is a new craft, and you'll be one of the people defining what good looks like.

Key responsibilities

- 

Set and hold the quality bar for every page on platform.claude.com/docs — clarity, correctness, completeness, voice

- 

Own the information architecture: structure the docs so developers and agents find what they need on the first try, and restructure when the product evolves underneath it

- 

Write and rewrite the highest-leverage pages yourself; review and edit contributions from product, engineering, and DevRel partners

- 

Own docs for new launches end-to-end, from early PRD through GA

- 

Write docs for agents as well as humans

- 

Ship code on the Claude API regularly so your understanding of the developer experience is firsthand, not secondhand

- 

Contribute to the claude-api skill, and author and maintain related docs-for-agents artifacts, defining how documentation should be written for LLM consumers

- 

Act as the primary customer of our internal docs-automation tooling, with a calibrated point of view on where Claude accelerates docs work and where human judgment is the bottleneck

- 

Build feedback loops from support tickets, community channels, and product analytics into docs improvements, and measure whether those improvements actually reduce confusion

- 

Partner closely with the DevX engineers who own the docs platform to shape the reading experience, navigation, search, and in-product docs surfaces

- 

Translate recurring developer friction into concrete product and API feedback when documentation alone can't fix it

Minimum qualifications

- 

You've been the end-to-end owner (not just a contributor) of a developer-facing surface like docs, SDKs, quickstarts, or a content program: setting a quality bar, holding it without being chased, and saying no to things that don't meet it

- 

You're an excellent technical writer. You can take a confusing page and make it clear, take a correct page and make it useful, and explain why each change made it better

- 

You have strong information architecture skills and can articulate why a docs site is structured well or badly within minutes of landing on it

- 

You're hands-on technical. You write and read code in at least one programming language, you've shipped working software on top of APIs, and you can hold your own in a design discussion with engineers

Preferred qualifications

- 

Background in developer relations, developer experience, developer education, or API product teams

- 

Experience owning docs or developer content at an API-first or developer-tools company

- 

Genuine curiosity about building with LLMs and a calibrated, non-hype view of what they're good at today

- 

Experience writing content intended for LLM consumption (skills, system prompts, retrieval corpora)

- 

Background in information architecture, UX writing, or content design

- 

Experience working with docs-as-code toolchains and contributing to docs infrastructure

- 

Public writing that demonstrates your voice (blog, newsletter, talks, open-source docs)

As those sites energize, their load needs contracted supply, and these contracts will be among the largest long-term commitments the energy team makes. You will set the supply plan for each market, take it to generators and suppliers, structure and negotiate the agreements, and carry them through internal approval to signature. This supply is also central to Anthropic's ratepayer-protection commitment, so what a deal does for other customers on the system counts alongside price and term. You will work beside the teammates who originate sites and behind-the-meter generation, who buy and transport gas, and who schedule the portfolio once it operates. You are this function's first dedicated owner.

Responsibilities:

- 

Own the front-of-meter supply plan for the United States: for each grid-connected site and market, how much load to contract, from whom, for how long, at what price structure, and by when, set against the site's ramp and the portfolio view of energy need.

- 

Take that plan to market. Build and keep relationships with generation owners, developers, independent power producers, and retail and wholesale suppliers; run competitive solicitations and bilateral negotiations; and compare offers on a like-for-like basis.

- 

Structure and negotiate PPAs, tolls, capacity agreements, and other long-term supply agreements from term sheet to signature, with legal and outside counsel: price and shape, delivery point and basis, congestion and curtailment, commercial operation dates and delay remedies for new-build projects, credit support, change in law, assignment, and termination.

- 

Make supply work under each market's rules: through retail providers and load-serving entities in competitive markets, and through utility tariffs, sleeved arrangements, and customer-sourced generation programs in regulated, cooperative, and public power territories. Work with the teammates who hold the utility relationship so the utility service agreement and the supply contract fit together.

- 

Design the supply portfolio to deliver Anthropic's ratepayer-protection commitment, and be able to show that it does: work with policy and outside analysts on how the effect on other customers is measured, and bring that test into deal selection and contract terms.

Collaborate with Energy Finance on deal valuation and the risk view behind it: forward curves, shape and basis risk, capacity and ancillary costs, counterparty credit, and development risk.

Carry commitments through internal approval: write the deal memo, state the price, the exposure, and the alternatives plainly, and answer questions from executives who do not work in energy.

Support negotiation of utility service agreements and large-load tariff terms for grid-connected sites, manage the interconnection and load-study process, and represent Anthropic in tariff proceedings and ISO/RTO rule changes alongside policy and industry coalitions.

Have 10+ years in power origination, structuring, or energy procurement, including PPAs or long-term supply contracts that you led from term sheet to signature.

Have bought power for a large load (a data center operator, industrial, utility, cooperative, or retail supplier), or have sold to those buyers and know what they should have asked for.

Know at least two US ISO/RTO markets (ERCOT, PJM, MISO, SPP, or others) well enough to price delivery point, basis, congestion, capacity, and ancillary costs into a deal, and understand how a large customer gets supply in a vertically integrated utility territory.

Can build and interrogate a deal valuation yourself, and can say what a fixed-price, shaped, index, or block structure does to the buyer's exposure.

- 

Read and mark up a PPA yourself. You use counsel well, and you do not hand them the commercial judgment.

- 

Understand credit support and project finance well enough to know what a developer's lenders need from an offtaker, and what that is worth in the negotiation.

- 

Write and speak plainly about large commitments to people outside energy, and coordinate well across teams that do not report to you: finance, legal, policy, site origination, and scheduling.

- 

Have built a book, a program, or a function from zero, and are comfortable moving quickly on incomplete information.

- 

Experience contracting supply for data centers or other large, fast-ramping load.

- 

Experience with firm and shaped products: storage-backed and hybrid structures, tolling agreements, and offtake from new-build dispatchable or clean firm generation.

- 

Experience in regulated and public power territories: sleeved PPAs, utility green or clean-transition tariffs, and large-load tariffs and the provisions in them that protect other ratepayers.

- 

Experience with virtual PPAs, energy attribute certificates, and hourly matching or emissions accounting.

- 

Experience with Canadian energy markets.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Every request that hits Claude — from claude.ai, the API, our cloud partners, or internal research — depends on a set of decisions made before it ever reaches a model: where each request should be served and how much capacity each model needs right now. Getting those decisions right is crucial to satisfying throughput, reliability, and latency constraints. This group builds the control plane that makes those decisions for Anthropic's inference fleet and own the inference request path.

This is a deeply technical group. The engineers here design placement and load-balancing algorithms, build quantitative models of demand, capacity, and system performance, improve latency across kernel, network, and framework boundaries, and reason carefully about how a change to the fleet ripples through everything that depends on it.

You'll lead a strong group of ML platform, infrastructure, and distributed-systems engineers working alongside the teams that build our ML internals and cloud infrastructure. You need enough systems depth to make architectural calls, hire people who go deep, and see when a proposed change will ripple across the fleet. You're accountable for the health of the whole path from request to model: its efficiency, its reliability, and how well it evolves as models, hardware, and clouds change underneath it.

Key responsibilities

- Own the technical roadmap for how the inference fleet is coordinated — where traffic goes, where capacity lives, how caches are placed, how fast the system reacts to demand, and the protocols that keep the control plane and the inference engines in sync

- Partner with the product, inference engine, performance, and capacity teams to identify throughput, latency, utilization, and cost wins, then turn those into shipped improvements with measurable results

- Build the group's habit of quantitative modeling: claim a win only when you can measure it, and know before you ship what the expected effect is

- Set technical strategy for how the control plane evolves across heterogeneous hardware, across multiple cloud providers, and across all our serving surfaces

- Run the group's operational backbone — on-call rotations, incident response, postmortem review, deploy safety — so the teams can ship aggressively without the system becoming fragile

- Create clarity at a seam: this group sits between the API surface, the inference engines, capacity planning, and the cloud deployment teams

- Develop and retain strong existing teams, and hire against a high technical bar

- Coach engineers through a roadmap where priorities shift

- Shape team structure as the scope grows: decide where the boundaries between problem areas should sit, and grow leads who can own each

- Pick up slack when it matters. These are small teams on a critical path; sometimes the EM is the one unblocking a stuck initiative or synthesizing a design debate

Minimum qualifications

- Engineering management experience leading teams on critical-path production infrastructure at scale

- A deep systems background — load balancing, scheduling, cluster orchestration, autoscaling, cache-coherent distributed state, high-performance networking, or similar — with enough depth to make architectural calls about how a large fleet is coordinated and to evaluate candidates who go to the kernel and framework level

- Experience shipping performance or efficiency improvements in large-scale systems, and the ability to explain, with numbers, what the impact was — including the cost side, not just the latency side

- Experience running production infrastructure with real operational stakes: on-call, incident response, capacity events, deploy discipline

- A results-oriented, impact-driven approach, and comfort working in a space where throughput, latency, cost, stability, launch timelines, and feature velocity all pull in different directions

- Ability to build strong relationships across team boundaries — this is a seam role, and much of the job is making sure other teams can rely on yours

- Curiosity about machine learning systems — you don't need an ML research background, but you should want to learn how transformer inference actually works and how that shapes the systems problems

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of engineering management experience

- Experience with LLM inference serving — KV caching, continuous batching, request scheduling, prefill/decode disaggregation

- Background in cluster schedulers, autoscalers, load balancers, service meshes, or fleet control planes at scale (Kubernetes internals, Borg-style systems, or equivalents)

- Experience running workloads across multiple clouds or partner platforms, and the reliability and cost trade-offs that come with it

- Familiarity with heterogeneous accelerator fleets and how hardware differences affect workload placement and rollout sequencing

- Experience leading teams at supercomputing or hyperscaler infrastructure scale

- Experience leading multiple teams or a group through rapid-growth periods where hiring, onboarding, and team splits competed with roadmap delivery

About Anthropic

About the team

The Integrity and Attestation team's remit is to prove what is running at Anthropic: what code it is, where it came from, and whether the machine underneath it is in a known-good state. We build the systems that cryptographically verify build artifacts, model weights, and machines, from hardware roots of trust through firmware and boot to the credentials a workload receives. We also secure the management plane of our servers. These controls protect our model weights and customer data across cloud providers and bare-metal AI data centers, including sites operated by partners.

We are hiring an Engineering Manager to lead this team. Anthropic is bringing up new compute quickly, across new hardware platforms and new partners, and each one has to meet the same bar. In this role you will set the team's charter, practices, and priorities. You will partner with our infrastructure, data center, and hardware teams, as well as outside vendors, so that integrity is designed in rather than added later. The goal is simple to state: a machine gets secrets and workloads only after it proves it should, and a new site reaches that bar without slowing down compute.

About the role

- Own the integrity roadmap: threat model from silicon and firmware up through the operating system and workloads, decide what to build, and deliver it

- Be able to reason about the design and implementation of remote attestation, measured and verified boot, hardware roots of trust (TPM, SPDM), machine identity, and the reference values that define known-good

- Make attestation the default path, so machines receive credentials and join clusters only after proving their firmware, system software, and security configuration, with no human in the loop

- Build provenance for what we deploy: signed build artifacts and model weights, independent verification, and tamper-evident transparency logs

- Lead the protection of sensitive data in use and at rest, including encryption and the chokepoints that control access to it

- Secure the server management plane across every site: scoped and audited access to baseboard management controllers and management of per-device credentials

- Make security repeatable as compute grows, so a new site or hardware platform inherits these controls in hours, not weeks

- Join compute bring-up, data center, and hardware teams at design time

- Define clear ownership with partner teams: when operations move to another team, your team keeps the security properties and can prove they still hold

- Own the integrity evidence for our security goals and compliance: the invariants hold, and you can prove it

- Hire, grow, and retain senior security software engineers; own their career development, and set the practices the team runs on as it scales

- Low ego, high empathy; has built diverse teams and has former reports who would vouch for them.

- Experience managing infrastructure or security engineering teams, including hiring, developing, and managing senior and staff engineers

- Has grown engineers into staff or lead roles, and experience with performance management

- Created and maintained a high performing in hypergrowth environments. Kept a team intact and delivering through reorgs, charter changes, or leadership turnover

- Experience owning a security or infrastructure domain end to end: setting multi-year strategy, delivering year-long cross-organizational work with little direction, and answering to executives for its risk and tradeoffs

- An appreciation for distributed systems and properties beyond security, including reliability, efficiency, and maintainability

- Scaled a team and its systems together through hypergrowth, where last quarter's architecture was already too small

- Hands-on engineering in at least one of: platform security, secure boot and firmware, hardware roots of trust, confidential computing, or software supply chain integrity

- Threat modeling and risk assessment for systems that span hardware and software, with strong security judgment and pragmatism

- Comfortable leading through ambiguity with multiple partner teams and outside vendors, where you don't control the hardware or the schedule

- At least 5+ years managing engineering teams and 8+ years hands-on in platform, infrastructure, or security engineering

- Built or operated remote attestation, device identity, or fleet-wide boot integrity at production scale

- Worked with BMCs, Redfish, GPU or accelerator attestation, or large-scale bare-metal provisioning

- Experience with Nitro, SEV-SNP, TDX, or similar confidential computing platforms

- Built signing, provenance, or transparency systems such as Sigstore, SLSA, or binary transparency

- Designed key management or offline ceremonies for high-value secrets

- Worked in high-assurance environments where controls had to be evidenced, not just deployed

- Taken infrastructure from zero to one and then to maturity: built the first version where nothing existed, then run and hardened it into a system other teams depend on

- Built or rebuilt a hiring loop and held the bar while adding headcount quickly

- Pragmatic and steady: cares about unblocking research, product and compute as much as a clean architecture, and brings patience and judgment to opinionated senior engineers

- Clear and persuasive communicator in writing and in person

- Familiarity with AI security and safety concepts

Engineering Manager, Labs
About the role
At Anthropic, we're building AI systems that are safe, beneficial, and transformative. Our mission is to develop AI that benefits humanity, and we believe the most powerful capabilities emerge when we thoughtfully bridge the gap between research breakthroughs and real-world applications.
Anthropic Labs serves as our internal accelerator. We're looking for the next breakout hits that bring substantial revenue or transform an industry. We operate in close partnership with research and build through fast iteration cycles. Past successes include Claude Code and MCP.
We're seeking an Engineering Manager to lead and grow our team of software engineers working on early-stage AI capabilities. You'll have an outsized impact in shaping how Anthropic builds world-class privacy into Claude from the ground up.

This is a role with extraordinary scope and leverage. You'll own a large subset of privacy engineering for Anthropic end-to-end. The work spans privacy-preserving architectures for AI training and inference, foundational data governance and lifecycle systems, and the automated controls that turn complex regulation into engineering reality. You'll lead a team of talented privacy engineers that builds and operates the platform and infra frameworks underpinning Anthropic's privacy and compliance posture. Your job is to scale the team and its charter as Anthropic grows. 

Working at the intersection of privacy engineering, AI safety, and distributed systems, your team will solve novel challenges in protecting user data at scale, handling billions of conversations while maintaining model quality and research velocity. If owning the whole problem and having an outsized impact on how a frontier AI lab protects its users sounds compelling, this role might be for you.

- 

Build and lead the team: Recruit, develop, and retain a team of exceptional privacy engineers; establish team charter, practices, and priorities as the team matures

- 

Drive technical strategy: Partner with technical leads, researchers, and legal to set direction for privacy infrastructure across training, inference, and product surfaces: data governance and policy enforcement, deletion and retention at scale, encryption and key management, audit and access transparency, and ML-based PII detection and redaction.
