Build foundational privacy infrastructure: Guide the team in building automated data discovery, classification, access controls, audit logging, and lifecycle management systems, plus data governance platforms for tracking lineage, purpose limitation, and retention across distributed AI systems

-

Anthropic's compute fleet is one of the largest and most varied in the world, and everything we do from training frontier models to serving Claude depends on getting the right work onto the right hardware at the right time. We build the scheduling layer for Anthropic's Kubernetes fleet, the tools researchers and engineers use to launch and manage their jobs, and the systems that make sure the fleet is used as efficiently as possible. postings.title: [Expression of Interest] Research Manager, Interpretability
postings.location: San Francisco, CA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
Note: we don't have open Research Manager positions on the Interpretability team at this time. However, we're actively growing our team of Research Engineers and Research Scientists. If you're excited about interpretability research and open to an individual contributor role, we encourage you to apply.

About the Interpretability team

When you see what modern language models are capable of, do you wonder, "How do these things work? How can we trust them?"

The Interpretability team’s mission is to reverse engineer how trained models work, and Interpretability research is one of Anthropic’s core research bets on AI safety. We believe that a mechanistic understanding is the most robust way to make advanced systems safe. 

People mean many different things by "interpretability". We're focused on mechanistic interpretability, which aims to discover how neural network parameters map to meaningful algorithms. Some useful analogies might be to think of us as trying to do "biology" or "neuroscience" of neural networks, or as treating neural networks as binary computer programs we're trying to "reverse engineer".

We aim to create a solid scientific foundation for mechanistically understanding neural networks and making them safe (see our vision post). We have focused on resolving the issue of "superposition" (see Toy Models of Superposition, Superposition, Memorization, and Double Descent, and our May 2023 update), which causes the computational units of the models, like neurons and attention heads, to be individually uninterpretable, and on finding ways to decompose models into more interpretable components. Our subsequent work which found millions of features in Claude 3.0 Sonnet, one of our production language models, represents progress in this direction. In our most recent work, we developed methods that allow us to build circuits using features and use these circuits to understand the mechanisms associated with a model's computation and study specific examples of multi-hop reasoning, planning, and chain-of-thought faithfulness on Claude Haiku 3.5, one of our production models.” This is a stepping stone towards our overall goal of mechanistically understanding neural networks.

A few places to learn more about our work and team are this introduction to Interpretability from our research lead, Chris Olah, Stanford CS25 lecture given by Josh Batson, and TWIML AI podcast with Emmanuel Ameisen.

Some of our team's notable publications include and our Circuits’ Methods and Biology papers, Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet, Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning, A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits, In-context Learning and Induction Heads, and Toy Models of Superposition. This work builds on ideas from members' work prior to Anthropic such as the original circuits thread, Multimodal Neurons, Activation Atlases, and Building Blocks.

About the role

Anthropic's compute runs on a growing global portfolio of data centers built with development partners. As a Senior Field Engineer on the Data Center Design and Engineering team, you will work side by side with developers, general contractors and engineers of record to resolve technical issues on site and speed up construction. You will spend most of your time on active sites, acting as our team's eyes, voice and technical judgment in the field. You will spot problems first, get the right people moving, and stay with each issue until it is closed.

You don't need a data center background. We care more about whether you have delivered complex industrial projects from the field and can get contractors and partners to act when you have no formal authority over them.

What you'll do

Be our engineering presence on site. You will walk installed work against the approved design and build working relationships with developers, general contractors, engineers of record, vendors and commissioning teams. You will hold design acceptance on our team's behalf, deciding whether installed work meets the design. When field conditions and drawings disagree, you will be the first call. You will settle what you can on the spot and bring in the right discipline engineer for the rest. More than 50% of your working time will be at project sites, often with overnight travel across multiple sites. The rest will be remote from your home base.

Get issues closed. You will keep one prioritized list of open engineering issues for your sites, each with an owner and a date. You will follow up in person, challenge dates that don't hold up, and escalate early with a clear recommendation when something is stuck.

Find out why things fail. When equipment, an installation or a test fails, you will gather the evidence, test the first explanation, and trace the failure to its underlying cause. You will confirm that the fix works and check whether other sites carry the same risk.

Clear the path to commissioning and handover. You will check the interfaces between power, cooling, controls and structure before they surface as test failures. You will drive RFIs, deviations and field changes to decisions, so that open engineering questions don't hold up the crews.

Bring the field back into the design. You will turn recurring site problems into changes to our designs, standards and audit checklists. Each project should make the next one easier to deliver.

What this role is not

You won't manage construction crews or direct contractors' means and methods; those stay with our construction delivery partners. You will work with our discipline engineers and hold the field view, rather than produce design documents.

- 

Have spent years on active project sites in energy, power, heavy industrial, data center or similar environments, as an engineer, project manager, or construction or commissioning lead

Can read drawings, single-line diagrams, P&IDs, specifications and schedules well enough to see where they disagree with what's been installed

Can give specific examples of persuading contractors, vendors or partners who didn't report to you to change course

Hold your position under pressure, back it with evidence, deliver bad news early, and change your mind when the facts change

Write short, factual reports that a busy reader can act on

Treat safety as your own job, and will stop work that isn't safe

- 

Worked in LNG, refining, offshore, power generation, semiconductor or naval environments

-

postings.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

AI is changing both sides of the security equation, and Anthropic is focused on putting frontier AI capabilities in the hands of defenders. Cybersecurity is a fast-growing area for Anthropic, spanning enterprise security teams that adopt Claude for their own security work and security companies that build their products on our models. The buyers are demanding and data-driven, from CISOs to hands-on practitioners in security engineering, application security, security operations, threat intelligence, and incident response.

As Field Marketing Lead, Cybersecurity, you will lead Anthropic's field marketing for the cybersecurity audience around the world, helping position Claude as the trusted AI partner for security teams. You will align closely with the sales organization, develop the marketing strategies and tools the field needs, and partner with Anthropic's cybersecurity experts in product marketing, solutions marketing, and across the business to turn their positioning and messaging into programs and campaigns. You will be the cybersecurity lead that our campaigns and regional field marketing teams draw on, working with customers in every segment and with a focus on expanding within existing accounts. You will make sure that how we show up to CISOs, practitioners, and the buying committee is credible, consistent, and tied to revenue, whether in a global campaign, an executive roundtable, or a flagship industry event.

Location: this is a global role, with a preference for candidates based in San Francisco or New York.

Key responsibilities

- Own the global cybersecurity field marketing plan: define how we reach CISOs, practitioners, and the buying committee in every customer segment, the annual program calendar, and the goals and success metrics agreed with sales leadership before budget is committed

- Align with the sales organization worldwide: agree on target accounts and buying committees, build programs that expand Anthropic's footprint in existing accounts and open new opportunities, and make sure account teams have what they need to invite, follow up, and convert

- Partner with product marketing, solutions marketing, and Anthropic's cybersecurity experts: build on their positioning, messaging, and enablement, and work with them to turn cyber use cases into the programs and campaigns that build awareness and demand

- Develop the marketing strategies and tools the field needs: playbooks, program kits, speaker guidance, and event recommendations that let regional field marketers in the Americas, EMEA, and APAC run cybersecurity programs locally without starting from scratch

- Design and run flagship cybersecurity moments in the field: executive roundtables, CISO dinners, practitioner workshops, and Anthropic's field presence around major industry events such as RSAC, Black Hat, Gartner Security & Risk Management Summit, and Infosecurity Europe, in step with the launch, content, and thought leadership plans led by product and solutions marketing

- Serve as the cybersecurity field lead for integrated campaigns: bring audience insight, field feedback, and program ideas, and extend global campaigns into regional programs so they land with CISOs, practitioners, and the rest of the buying committee

- Bring the voice of the security buyer back into Anthropic: share what you hear from customers, analysts, and the field with Product, Sales, and Marketing leadership

- Measure what matters: sourced and influenced pipeline, expansion within existing accounts, program-level attribution, and a clear read on which programs earn more investment, built with Marketing Ops

- Protect the brand with a skeptical audience: hold a high bar for technical accuracy, keep the story focused on defenders and responsible deployment, avoid fear-based messaging, and know when to say no to a program that would not earn trust

- Operate as connective tissue across Anthropic: Sales, Campaigns, regional Field Marketing, Product Marketing, Solutions Marketing, Partner Marketing, Partnerships, Events, and Comms all touch this audience. You keep them coordinated and the customer experience coherent

Minimum qualifications

- Working fluency in the cybersecurity landscape, across areas such as security operations, detection and response, threat intelligence, application security, vulnerability management, cloud security, and governance, risk and compliance, with enough technical depth to hold a credible conversation with both CISOs and hands-on practitioners

- A track record of partnering with sales teams on pipeline and on expansion within existing accounts, including account-based programs and executive engagement, with results to show for them

- Experience across both integrated campaigns and field marketing, and the judgment to know which one a given goal calls for

- Experience operating globally: you have led programs across multiple regions and enabled local teams to run them well

- Strong influence without authority: able to set direction for campaigns and regional field marketers who do not report to you

- Comfort building in ambiguity: the playbook for this motion is being written now, and you'll write much of it

About the role

Finance systems are critical to how Anthropic operates and scales. As the Finance Systems Production Support Lead, you will set the strategy for how we support those systems, bringing operational rigor and one consistent support model across the finance portfolio.

You will lead a lean support team with US and international coverage, set the service levels Finance can rely on, and make sure each incident leaves the systems stronger than it found them.

This is also a chance to redefine what production support looks like, using Claude to scale and transform how we support finance systems. Claude will handle more of the routine work over time, and you will own the exceptions, the quality bar and the patterns that feed back into the product roadmap. This team will cover our core platforms, including homegrown systems and applications built on Claude.

Responsibilities

- Own the support model: Build one operating model for tickets, access and incidents across finance applications, including ERP, close, procure to pay, revenue, planning, tax and treasury systems, plus new internally built applications.

- Lead a lean support team: Manage the support team day to day, including capacity, performance and escalation paths. You will also be the team's backup, working tickets and incidents yourself as needed.

- Design the rotation and operating rigor: Design the US and international support rotation, including close-week coverage and handoffs. Set the routines that keep support consistent, such as triage, runbooks, postmortems and regular service reviews.

- Drive operational excellence: Shape lean, scalable support processes that grow with the business, and implement leading practices across how the team works.

- Build training and onboarding: Create the training and onboarding that gets new support team members productive quickly and prepares Finance users for new systems and releases.

- Set and meet service levels: Define SLAs by priority and category, run triage, and plan coverage around month-end and quarter-end close.

- Run incidents and root cause analysis: Lead sensitive and time-critical production issues from first response to communication with Finance leaders, then drive root causes to a fix so they don't recur.

- Own release management: Run release testing and deployment across the portfolio, including Workday's twice-yearly releases. Partner with Product Owners on what to test, and put test automation ahead of added headcount.

- Run support by the metrics: Report ticket volume, time to resolve, SLA attainment, defects that escape a release, and automation coverage. Use the data to drive decisions, and turn the trends into input for each product roadmap.

- Make support audit-ready: Work with Product Owners and Internal Audit so tickets, access changes, support-run changes and runbooks hold up to SOX and public company expectations.

- Run recurring user access reviews: Own the recurring user access review cycle across finance applications, with evidence that stands up to audit.

Minimum qualifications

- Experience running production support for enterprise finance applications, ideally including Workday Financials or a comparable ERP, in a live, high-volume environment

- Experience leading a lean support function, including coverage across time zones

- Experience shaping lean, scalable support processes using leading practices, including SLAs, triage, incident management, root cause analysis and runbooks, and running them with metrics that leaders actually use

- Knowledge of how finance works day to day, including close, procure to pay

- Understanding of SOX controls for change management and user access, including recurring access reviews, and the ability to produce evidence that stands up to audit

- Experience leading release management, including testing and deployment, with a practical view on what to automate first

- Ability to stay calm and clear under pressure, and to explain an incident and its risk to both accountants and engineers

- Hands-on skills: reading an integration error, querying data with SQL and digging into a ticket yourself when that's what it takes

Anthropic's customers renew on a mix of committed and consumption contracts, and the number of renewals is growing faster than any team of people could keep pace with. We don't want to answer that by hiring hundreds of renewal managers. We want renewals to run as a system: Claude and agents do most of the work, from spotting risk to drafting the offer to closing a standard renewal in product, and people step in where judgment, negotiation or relationships matter.

You'll design, build and run that system. You'll own the renewal outcome for the business globally and the product and technology that delivers it. You'll lead a small team of builders and the human layer, internal specialists and outsourced partners, that handles what agents can't yet. You'll work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Deal Desk, Finance, Billing and Product Engineering.

What you'll own in your first year

- The design of the renewal system: which work agents run end to end, which work goes to a person, and the handoff rules between them.

- A standard renewal that needs no person: a Claude-generated offer in product ahead of term end, accepted and provisioned automatically, with anything outside guidance routed to a seller with a recommended quote.

- The data the system runs on: contract, commit burndown and usage data clean enough that agents and people trust it, built with Billing and Finance.

- Early-warning signals for consumption risk and commitment shortfall, and what happens when one fires.

- The human layer: how internal specialists, outsourced partners and account teams work around the agents, and the measures they're held to.

- The next large renewal cycles, run with fewer manual steps per renewal than today.

- Weekly renewal and retention forecasts grounded in usage and contract data.

- Executive renewal conversations on the largest and most complex accounts, alongside account teams.

- Owned renewal, retention or post-sale outcomes at large scale, either running the function or leading the product or service that runs it for others.

About the Team

Foragers is a new Field Services team within our physical infrastructure organization. We're the boots on the ground for Anthropic's physical infrastructure: the people who get hardware into racks, gear commissioned, and sites handed over. The team is being stood up now, so early hires shape how we operate. This role is the lab-focused counterpart to our traveling field engineers. Your mission is to ensure our hardware labs are functional, useful, and ready to support the growing number of teams and projects that need access to physical hardware. This includes both standard hardware (think typical accelerator setups) and more specialized ones like ensuring our security teams have access to all the right headers and other hardware instrumentation on the machines.

Understanding and anticipating the needs of the various teams that rely on the labs will be another critical part of this role. - Enough Linux and networking (VLANs, DHCP, DNS, basic switch config) to take a bare machine to a state a remote engineer can use

- Have managed vendors, contractors, quotes, and freight for physical equipment

- Work independently with minimal supervision , and know when to ask

postings.title: Hardware Systems Architect
postings.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Anthropic trains and serves frontier AI models on some of the largest and most diverse accelerator fleets in the world, and the hardware those models run on is one of the most direct levers we have on capability, cost, and reliability. Our Hardware Systems team owns the system-level architecture of that compute — from the package boundary out through boards, racks, interconnect, power, cooling, and the datacenter interface.

We're hiring senior hardware systems architects and technical leads who can work broadly across the hardware stack and go deep where it's needed, and who have the judgment to make and own directional calls — what to build, what to buy, what to co-design with a partner. You'll set architecture, write the specs that partners and internal teams build against, and own the validation and qualification strategy that proves the result.

The skillsets we need span power, cooling, mechanical, interconnect, signal integrity, data and control plane, system management, reliability and serviceability — applied across networking, compute, storage, and accelerator systems.

You'll work closely with our ML performance, infrastructure software, supply chain, and datacenter teams, and directly with hardware vendors and partners across the stack. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a genuine collaborator — we expect this team to push on what AI-assisted hardware design and review can look like.

Key responsibilities

- Own system path-finding and architecture for your domain across the breadth of compute Anthropic deploys — from concept and requirements through spec, design review, and deployment — and act as a reviewer and thought partner across the others.

- Write and own high-level requirements and specifications — system, board, interface, rack — that partners and internal teams build against.

- Review partner and vendor designs against our requirements, make the build / buy / co-design calls with supply chain and partnership teams, and surface misalignment or schedule risk early enough to act on it.

- Drive the interconnect and networking architecture that ties our systems together — scale-up and scale-out fabrics, NICs and switches, optics, and topology.

- Drive board-, chassis-, and system-level architecture with our partners — major component placement, PCB architecture, connector and cable design, and power and thermal budgeting — at the chassis, rack, and data-hall level.

- Develop performance simulations, hardware models, and "what-if" scenarios to evaluate and choose between candidate hardware architectures.

- Define validation, bring-up, and qualification strategy for new platforms — including the telemetry and reliability targets they need to hit in the fleet — and track the technology roadmaps and vendor landscape that shape what we deploy in the short and long term.

- Partner with ML performance and infrastructure software teams so hardware decisions land well for the workloads that actually run on them.

- Help shape how hardware engineering operates at Anthropic — develop and apply AI-assisted approaches to design, spec review, and validation; establish review forums, spec standards, and partner engagement.

Minimum qualifications

- Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one core hardware-systems domain (e.g., interconnect, power, thermal) for large-scale compute or networking systems.

- Experience owning hardware system architecture at scale — machine, rack, row, and cluster — and authoring specifications and requirements.

- Experience taking hardware from architecture through bring-up and high-volume production deployment.

- Experience working with external hardware vendors and partners — reviewing their designs and holding them to a specification.

- Ability to reason about trade-offs across adjacent hardware domains (e.g., interconnect ↔ power ↔ thermal ↔ mechanical) rather than within a single one.

- Track record of technical leadership — owning directional decisions and their consequences, and driving alignment across teams and partners.

- Comfort operating with high autonomy and limited process in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

- Strong written communication — you'll write specs and reviews that many teams depend on.

Preferred qualifications

Anthropic is building data center capacity across many sites at once, and for every site we own or lease we have committed to invest significantly in the host community, on terms we can stand behind publicly.

We're looking for someone to own our community benefits program end to end, across an international portfolio of many sites, so that every commitment is tracked, funded, paid on schedule and publicly reported. You'll negotiate the community-benefit terms with developers and other counterparties, from the term sheet through the lease, then manage those developers after signature, run the payouts and publish each site's yearly reports.

You'll work closely with our data center deal team, Finance, Legal and Policy. Our Community Engagement Managers own on-the-ground community relationships and community benefits agreements with local governments; this role owns the program end to end, including the deal terms behind it.

Own the commitments ledger: every community commitment, budget and payout at every site, and who holds the money

Track payment schedules and rent recovery against each site's construction milestones, with Finance

Manage developers after lease signature: make sure they actually hold and pay out community funds at our direction, send their data on time, and troubleshoot issues when they arise

Run payouts: check who receives the money, run select programs, such as the electricity credit, through an outside partner, and publish who got what each year

Track what is committed, signed, funded and paid, and where a deal is stuck

Keep the terms we sign consistent with our public commitments

Build and hire the team that runs this function on an ongoing basis

Deals

Negotiate the community-benefit terms in developer leases and capacity agreements: who funds the community commitment, whether it sits on the developer's books or is recovered through rent, and when payments are made during construction

- 

Work the term sheets with developers and other counterparties, and partner with our data center deal team so these terms are in every new deal and expansion from the start

- 

Time each site's community commitments to its schedule: as early as the day after lease execution, and no later than substantial completion

- 

Build and maintain standard form templates for the community commitments and leases, so each new deal starts from an agreed position

Have owned a program or portfolio end to end across many sites or deals, and kept named owners to dates

Have negotiated incentive, tax and community commitments with state and local governments for new sites, and closed them as signed agreements

Have worked with state and local officials across many markets, and know what it takes to get an agreement approved

- 

Have worked in economic development for a data center operator or other large infrastructure developer, on the company's side of the table

- 

Are fluent in the financial side: funds, payment schedules, how a cost is recovered through rent, and what sits on whose books

- 

Write clear term sheets and clear updates for executives

- 

Are comfortable building a function from scratch, quickly and with ambiguity

- 

Care about Anthropic's mission and about doing right by the communities that host our infrastructure

Experience negotiating community benefits agreements

Experience in government relations or public affairs

Deal experience outside the US (for example, Canada or Australia)

postings.description:

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

As Head of Customer Success, APAC at Anthropic, you will build and lead our Customer Success function across Asia Pacific. You will scale a team of managers and CSMs who help our most strategic APAC customers realize the full value of Claude. This is a foundational leadership role: you will establish how we run CS in the region, hire and develop a multi-market team of managers, and partner closely with your global counterparts to deliver a globally consistent customer experience while localising where it matters.

APAC is not one market. You will lead across India, Japan, Korea, ASEAN, and Australia and New Zealand (ANZ), each with its own buying culture, regulatory context, language needs and pace of AI adoption. You will work hand-in-hand with global GTM, Product and Engineering leaders to shape our APAC CS strategy, take APAC customer priorities back into the business, and drive adoption, retention and growth across some of the most exciting markets in the world.

Key responsibilities

- Build and lead a multi-layered Customer Success organisation across APAC, managing managers and scaling the team responsibly as our APAC business grows.

- Define and execute the APAC CS strategy in close partnership with global CS leadership, aligning with the global agenda while localising approach, motion and programmes for APAC market dynamics.

- Own CS business outcomes including customer health, retention, expansion and satisfaction across APAC accounts.

- Hire, develop and coach a high-performing team of CS managers and individual contributors, building a culture that reflects Anthropic's values across Asia's diverse geographies, languages and working cultures.

- Partner with global CS, Sales, Product and Engineering teams so the voice of APAC customers reaches decision-making forums.

- Establish scalable processes, playbooks and operating cadences that work across APAC time zones (India to Japan, Korea and ANZ) and overlap responsibly with global teams.

- Represent Anthropic with senior customer stakeholders across APAC, leading executive engagements, QBRs and strategic account conversations with enterprises, digital natives, startups and public sector bodies.

- Build strong working relationships with APAC channel and cloud partners, and with systems integrators and consulting firms that shape enterprise AI adoption in the region.

- Contribute to global CS strategy as a senior leader, bringing an APAC perspective to team planning, segmentation and prioritisation.

- Help shape how we deploy AI responsibly with customers across APAC's varied regulatory environments, including data residency, privacy and sector rules in markets such as India, Japan, Korea, Singapore and Australia.

Minimum qualifications

- 15+ years of experience in management consulting, technology consulting, professional services or customer-facing advisory roles, with a track record of advising senior client executives on complex transformation programmes.

- Experience building and leading multi-market Customer Success or Technical Success organisations, including managing managers

- Track record of scaling CS teams across APAC at enterprise software, SaaS or AI/ML companies

- Demonstrated ability to balance global alignment with regional localisation across multiple APAC markets and cultures.

- Strong people leadership: a clear philosophy on hiring, coaching and developing managers and senior ICs.

- Experience owning enterprise customer relationships and driving measurable business outcomes (retention, expansion, adoption) in APAC markets.

- Strong executive presence and the ability to represent a company credibly with C-suite stakeholders across APAC.

- Excellent cross-functional partnership skills, particularly working across time zones with global leadership teams.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience leading Customer Success across APAC

En tant que responsable de deuxième niveau de l’équipe Applied AI Industries pour l’Europe du Sud et le Moyen-Orient chez Anthropic, vous stimulerez l’adoption de l’IA de pointe en partenariat avec le reste de l’organisation commerciale (go-to-market). Nos clients Industries en France, dans la péninsule Ibérique et en Italie comptent parmi les plus grandes entreprises de la région, dans les services financiers, la santé et les sciences de la vie, l’industrie manufacturière, les télécommunications, la distribution, l’énergie et d’autres secteurs. Vous vous appuierez sur votre expérience de la création et du management d’équipes d’avant-vente technique pour favoriser une transformation positive par l’IA, qui réponde aux besoins métier de nos clients et à leurs exigences techniques et réglementaires, tout en offrant un haut niveau de fiabilité et de sécurité.

Vous dirigerez et développerez l’équipe d’architectes de solutions qui travaille avec les account executives pour aider les entreprises à adopter et à déployer les produits d’Anthropic, notamment Claude Cowork, Claude Code et la Claude Development Platform (notre API). Vous mettrez à profit vos compétences techniques et votre expérience de la vente consultative pour recruter d’excellents managers de premier niveau et contributeurs individuels, mettre en place les processus nécessaires au passage à l’échelle de votre équipe et représenter directement Anthropic lors d’échanges stratégiques avec les clients. Votre équipe couvrant simultanément plusieurs pays et secteurs, il vous reviendra d’aborder de manière stratégique les comptes complexes et d’identifier et de déployer des solutions adaptées à chaque marché, avec sa langue, sa culture d’entreprise et son contexte réglementaire.

About the role

The world's engineers want to get the most out of Claude. At Anthropic, technical instruction already happens everywhere: our Applied AI and Forward Deployed Engineering teams teach customers and partners, and engineers across the company help others learn to build with Claude. Today that instruction is a shared responsibility, delivered alongside people's primary roles. As demand grows, we need to turn that distributed expertise into a dedicated technical instruction function.

You will build that function.

You will be the first person at Anthropic whose full-time job is technical instruction. You'll spend your first year primarily in the classroom teaching engineers, architects, and other technical practitioners. You'll also build the people, standards, and systems that let Anthropic's technical instruction scale far beyond the people we directly employ.

This is a player-coach role. From day one you manage a small bench of instructors. You set the bar for what "ready to teach" means, decide who is cleared to teach a given module in Anthropic's technical programs, and assess facilitators from our training partners against that bar.

You're an engineer who teaches and a teacher who has led other teachers. You can build an agent live in front of a skeptical engineer, diagnose what isn't working in a technical lab, and make the material better. You can also watch an experienced instructor teach, tell them their session isn't ready yet, and coach them to get there.

You will report to the Head of Technical Enablement. The role is based in San Francisco with some travel expected.

Key responsibilities

- Lead from the front. Teach hands-on sessions to new Applied AI engineers, our field teams, and partner cohorts, in rooms from 12-person labs to 100-person training days.

- Build the instructor bench. Hire and develop instructors and curriculum developers. Decide contract renewals, and recommend conversions to full-time, against criteria you define.

- Set the quality bar. Own the observation rubric, dry-run protocol, and cleared-to-teach process for every instructor-led technical session.

- Scale through train-the-trainer. Set the bar the Lead Technical Instructor's train-the-trainer program teaches to, for internal experts, contract instructors, and partner facilitators.

- Turn expertise into instruction. Turn internal experts' content into sessions and labs that work in a live room.

- Enable programs without owning them. Staff other teams' programs with cleared instructors, and own the quality of instruction inside them.

- Measure and improve. Report learner pass rates per instructor each month, and act on them.

Minimum qualifications

- 8+ years of relevant professional experience across software engineering, solutions engineering, developer advocacy, technical education, or related technical roles.

- 4+ years of hands-on technical instruction. You have taught engineers live and hands-on, across audience sizes.

- Production engineering. You have written and shipped production software and engage credibly with experienced engineers on architecture and debugging.

- Recent hands-on AI development. In your last three years of work, you have built or debugged applications with LLM APIs, agent frameworks, tool use, MCP, or similar.

- People leadership. You have managed instructors, trainers, developer advocates, or solutions engineers, including hiring and performance management, and kept teaching.

- Instructor development. You have designed or run a train-the-trainer program, instructor certification, or observation framework.

- San Francisco location. You are based in San Francisco or willing to relocate with our relocation support, can be in the office every day a program runs, 3 days in a normal week, and can travel 25 to 30 percent.

Preferred qualifications

- A portfolio of sessions you taught and a rubric or certification you designed, shared only if you have the right.

- Experience building an instruction or developer-education function from scratch.

- Experience managing a contractor instructor bench, or clearing instructors across regions from recordings or trained observers.

- Daily use of Claude Code or a comparable agentic coding tool, or building on Claude through Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or Microsoft Foundry.

postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the Role 

The Detection & Response (D&R) team plays a critical role in protecting our systems, users, and data from security threats. We’re looking for an experienced Technical Program Manager to own and evolve incident management within D&R. This is a senior-level specialization on the Technical Program Manager ladder, focused on how we detect, respond to, and learn from security and operational incidents.

You’ll be the driving force behind maturing and scaling our incident response lifecycle—from detection and triage through containment, remediation, and post-incident review. Critically, some of the highest-impact work in this role happens after the immediate response: gathering data on incident trends, reporting on patterns and root causes, and working cross-functionally across engineering, security, infrastructure, and product teams to ensure that broad fixes and systemic improvements are actually implemented. 

You won’t just manage incidents—you’ll make sure we get meaningfully better after each one.

Responsibilities

- Own the end-to-end D&R incident management program: detection workflows, response processes, escalation paths, communication standards, and remediation tracking.

- Serve as incident commander for security incidents, driving clear coordination across executive, engineering, security, legal, and other appropriate stakeholders.

- Establish and run incident commander rotations within D&R, ensuring clear ownership and effective coordination during incidents of varying severity.

- Drive post-incident accountability by defining how action items are captured, assigned, tracked, and completed across teams—ensuring follow-through on both tactical fixes and strategic improvements.

- Gather, analyze, and report on incident trends and patterns to surface systemic risks, recurring root causes, and areas where the organization is most vulnerable.

- Translate trend analysis into actionable cross-functional initiatives: partner with engineering, infrastructure, security, and product teams to prioritize and implement broad fixes and preventive improvements that address root causes rather than symptoms.

- Lead incident review forums (post-mortems, retrospectives) and ensure learnings are captured, socialized, and acted upon across the organization.

- Develop and maintain D&R incident response documentation, playbooks, runbooks, and training materials; keep them current as the threat landscape and our systems evolve.

- Partner with detection engineering to improve alert fidelity, reduce noise, and shorten time-to-detection for security events.

- Define, develop, and track incident management KPIs and report regularly to D&R and Security leadership.

- Support broad cross-functional training and initiatives to uplevel security awareness across the company (e.g. Tabletop exercises, training, talks).

You may be a good fit if you:

- Have 7+ years of experience in technical program management, incident management, or security operations, with significant time spent in a detection & response or security incident response context.

- Have led or built incident response programs at a technology company, ideally in a high-growth or security-intensive environment.

- Have a demonstrated track record of turning incident data into organizational improvements—not just writing post-mortems, but driving the cross-functional work to implement systemic fixes.

- Are comfortable participating in on-call responsibilities and leading incident response during high-severity security events, including off-hours.

- Have experience building and scaling operational processes from the ground up in environments where structure didn’t previously exist.

- Excel at driving accountability and follow-through across multiple teams without direct authority—you know how to influence, track, and close the loop.

- Have strong analytical skills and experience with incident trend analysis, metrics reporting, and data-driven prioritization.

- Are highly organized with a knack for bringing structure to ambiguous, fast-moving situations.

- Have excellent communication skills, especially under pressure and when coordinating across technical and non-technical stakeholders, including executive leadership.

- Thrive in fast-paced environments where priorities shift and you’re often working with incomplete information.

Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Anthropic's infrastructure fleet spans a growing set of clouds, neoclouds, and on-prem sites. Every part of it is expanding rapidly. - Qualify each incoming capacity tranche against the forecast before signature: right shape, region, quarter, and supporting-resource envelope (storage, egress, CPU).

- Direct experience with cloud or neocloud providers on reserved-capacity onboarding, private offers, or capacity commitments.

postings.location: San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

We are looking for an experienced accountant to own Equity Accounting and Reporting at Anthropic, based in San Francisco. You will be the one owner of equity accounting numbers across US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP in every jurisdiction where we have employees holding equity: expense booking by entity, intercompany recharge booking, current and deferred tax on equity, and the equity footnote and local statutory disclosures, prepared once and reused. You will own equity reporting data from Shareworks, our equity administration platform, through to the ledgers, while staying hands-on: preparing and reviewing close materials, owning your own accounts, and serving as the first escalation point for the judgment calls in your domain.

Share-based compensation (SBC) is one of the most cross-functional areas of our reporting. Grants, vesting, exercises and the events that follow each carry requirements for US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP expense, pushdown and recharge postings, tax provisioning, payroll withholding, transfer pricing and statutory disclosure, and those needs are met across Equity Administration, Equity Reporting, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Transfer Pricing and Global Payroll from a single set of award-level records. This is a build role: you will take the open workstreams from manual to automated, work with Finance Systems and Shareworks to build the reports each stage needs, finalize the policies and agreements that sit behind recharges, and bring the end-to-end process to a scalable, efficient and fully compliant close. We are looking for someone who has owned equity accounting in a growing global organization before and wants to do it again at one of the most important companies in the world.

Key responsibilities

Close ownership

- 

Own the equity portfolio through month-end and quarter-end close: US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP equity expense, pushed down and booked by entity, including reconciliations, journal entries and variance commentary

- 

Own intercompany recharge booking: invoicing, settlement, Treasury communication and the foreign exchange (FX) that follows

- 

Own current and deferred tax on equity by entity and in local currency, including the IFRS deferred tax mark to the share price and windfalls or shortfalls through the tax provision

- 

Ensure every close deliverable is audit-ready, with clear documentation of positions and supporting evidence

Technical accounting and policy

- 

Write, own and maintain the accounting policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for equity across US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP: grant-date fair value and expense schedules, recharge basis by entity, mobility apportionment, and the treatment of cancellations, modifications and one-off events

- 

Partner closely with Tax to close every open policy position and execute the recharge agreements that depend on them

- 

Research the tax and accounting rules for each new jurisdiction entered and categorize it under our framework before the first grant lands there

- 

Own the equity footnote and local statutory disclosures for all entities, including the award rollforward for each period with internal transfers, and the external audit responses that support them

Controls

- 

Design and operate Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) controls across equity expense, recharges and deferred tax; review control evidence and own timely remediation of any gaps

- 

Establish completeness and cut-off controls so that the same award, the same entity, the same event dates and the same FX rate flow from Shareworks to every ledger, report and return

Systems and automation

- 

Anticipate changes in reporting needs and work with Finance Systems and Shareworks to build them: IFRS expense and deferred tax reports in local currency at Workday rates, mobility snapshots driving expense apportionment, corporate tax apportionment rules, and exercise and disclosure reports with mobility detail

- 

Automate the monthly pushdown and recharge postings and the reconciliation of deferred tax to expense reports, replacing manual work

- 

Document workflows and controls in a way that supports knowledge transfer, audit evidence and scale

Cross-functional partnership

- 

Partner with Equity Administration, Equity Reporting, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Transfer Pricing and Global Payroll so each stage of an award is handled from every statutory and reporting perspective and every stakeholder has the data they need

- 

Record in the local books (secondary ledgers) the local SBC expense and recharges that feed the cost base for transfer pricing

- 

Translate complex equity accounting into plain language for non-finance stakeholders

Equity events

- 

Lead the cross-functional, cross-jurisdictional review of one-off equity events such as tender offers and share repurchases, covering the accounting, the deduction, payroll withholding, Treasury and the resulting disclosures

- 

Coordinate with Tax and advisers on open conclusions, such as the apportionment logic for corporation tax versus payroll tax, so report configurations are right before they are built, manual rework is minimized and the data serves every purpose it is built for

Minimum qualifications

- 

Certified Public Accountant (CPA) or equivalent professional accounting qualification

- 

Deep, hands-on experience with stock-based compensation under Accounting Standards Codification Topic 718 (ASC 718), IFRS 2 and local GAAP, including equity roll-forwards and reconciliation to an equity administration platform

- 

Experience with the tax accounting for equity: current and deferred tax by entity, mobility apportionment, and windfalls and shortfalls through the provision

- 

Experience owning a portfolio of accounts through close in a public company or pre-initial public offering (IPO) environment, including designing and operating SOX controls

- 

Experience writing and maintaining accounting policies and SOPs, and being accountable for how they are applied

- 

Ability to structure ambiguous problems, reach defensible conclusions and document them clearly

- 

Clear written and verbal communication with non-accounting partners

Preferred qualifications

- 

Progressive accounting experience that combines Big 4 audit with time at a high-growth or startup company

- 

A clear point of view on how artificial intelligence (AI) tools can eliminate low-value accounting work, and a track record of putting it into practice

- 

A project management qualification or experience running cross-functional workstreams

postings.title: IT Support Engineer, Executive Support
postings.location: San Francisco, CA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the Role

We're standing up a dedicated executive support function within IT, and we're hiring the IT Support Engineer who will build it. IT Support is the front door for every employee technology need at Anthropic, and this role creates its most visible lane: white-glove support for our executives, their administrative business partners (ABPs), and our board.

You'll define what that service looks like: the support model for execs, board, and ABPs, the runbooks behind it, the intake and escalation paths, and the trusted relationships with ABPs and exec staff that make it work. You'll set the bar for discretion and polish as you go. You'll also be the person our leadership reaches when technology gets in the way. The requests that land in this lane range from routine to highly sensitive, and many arrive urgent: an executive locked out minutes before a meeting, an AV issue in a room full of leadership, a board member who needs setup handled quietly and correctly the first time. You own the request end to end and pull in specialist functions or IT Engineering pods as needed.

Responsibilities

- Stand up the executive support intake channels and run it: monitor, respond, and follow through on every request from executives, ABPs, and board members

- Define the white-glove service model for discretion-sensitive asks and deliver to it, holding confidentiality under pressure

- Design the board-meeting AV support playbook with the AV pod, and provide AV support for executive rooms and board meetings, from setup and pre-checks through live triage

- Create exec-support runbooks and SLAs that keep the service consistent as it grows

- Build trusted relationships with ABPs and executive staff, and establish clear intake paths so leadership knows exactly where to go

- Handle ABP escalations and exec-urgent issues calmly, and route into specialist lanes or IT Engineering pods when a request needs them

- Establish the board member device, account, and access setup process with our Onboarding lane

- Work the shared ticket queue with the SF Core team: walk-ups, desk-side help, hardware swaps, it-assist overflow, and AV T1 triage

- Participate in the Core on-call rotation and contribute to the knowledge base and runbooks

- Maintain a regular on-site presence in San Francisco 

You may be a good fit if you have

- 7+ years of experience in IT support and 3+ years in executive support

- Experience standing up a service or program from scratch, such as an executive support desk, a VIP support function, or a white-glove service

- Experience supporting executives, their assistants, or a board to a white-glove standard

- A track record of handling sensitive requests with discretion, and the judgment to know what stays confidential without being told

- Strong hands-on IT support fundamentals: macOS-primary fleets, identity and access, SaaS troubleshooting, hardware lifecycle

- AV fluency for executive rooms and board meetings: you can set up, verify, and fix a room under time pressure

- Composure when an urgent escalation lands, and the judgment to know when to pull in help

- High polish and low ego: you take pride in service quality and still pick up whatever the team needs, including the ordinary queue work

- A security-first mindset and excellent judgment about when user experience yields to security requirements

- Comfort with ambiguity: you can make progress before the process exists, and you enjoy shaping how things should work

- The instinct to write things down: runbooks, KB articles, and status updates that keep people informed

Nice to have

- Experience supporting a C-suite or board of directors at a company with significant security or compliance requirements

Anthropic’s engineers are building some of the most ambitious AI systems and applications in the world. We also help engineers, architects, and technical practitioners across Anthropic, our partners, and our customers learn to build with Claude.

Until now, technical instruction has largely been a shared responsibility. We are building a dedicated technical instruction function to make that learning exceptional and ensure that everyone who teaches in Anthropic’s technical programs meets a consistent, high bar.

We are looking for a Technical Instructor Lead in New York to help bring that standard to life. About half of your time will be spent delivering ILT hands-on technical instruction in New York and remotely across European time zones. - Instructor development experience. You have helped other instructors or technical presenters improve through observation, structured feedback, practice teaching, or train-the-trainer programs.

- Experience designing or operating a train-the-trainer, instructor certification, or observer-calibration program.

Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a world-class research group focused on making fundamental biological discoveries. The team combines cutting-edge AI with hands-on biological research, positioning Anthropic at the forefront of AI-accelerated scientific discovery.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape how AI transforms biological research. We are looking for an experienced leader to take responsibility for how our research gets executed, across every program and field we work in.

AI is making it much faster to generate scientific ideas, and testing them is now the harder problem. As our Life Sciences Operator for research, you'll be a key partner to our research teams, who work across many fields of biology. You'll build the relationships, the team, and the systems that turn their ideas into results quickly and to a high scientific standard.

You'll help build our approach to operationalizing science. The ideal candidate is self-directed and has built a career in organizations that hold a high bar for scientific and operational rigor.

Key responsibilities

- Turn research ideas into well-scoped experimental plans with clear milestones and criteria for success

- Select and manage the external partners best placed to run each project, and coordinate work that spans more than one

- Build a team of internal and external experts with the breadth the science requires

- Manage a large portfolio of concurrent projects and see each one through with speed and ownership

- Keep research leadership informed on progress, turnaround time, and outcomes

- Orchestrate research agendas with Claude and our internal agent frameworks

- Build insights into where AI-driven research planning works and where it falls short, and share them with the model-improvement and product teams as evaluations, datasets, and failure cases

Minimum qualifications

- Experience at a contract research organization (CRO), biotech, or pharmaceutical company, accountable for delivering experimental programs for other scientists from scoping to final data

- Established record of scoping, placing, and managing outsourced experimental work with several CROs at once, from either the sponsor side or the CRO side

- Ability to take an idea from outside your own field, find the right expert, and judge whether a plan is executable and sensibly scoped

- Experience running many projects in parallel, and the ability to show how you tracked, prioritized, and reported on them

- Use of AI tools as a default part of how you work, and interest in finding out how far that can go

- Comfort navigating ambiguity and developing solutions in rapidly evolving research environments

- Results orientation, with a bias towards flexibility and impact

- Existing working relationships with CROs across several experimental areas, and a network you can call on to find new ones

- Experience as a study director or project lead at a CRO, or leading external research at a biotech or pharmaceutical company

About the role

Anthropic's Integrity & Compliance team helps the company meet its legal and regulatory obligations as our products, customers, and global footprint grow. We're looking for a Manager, Compliance & Regulatory Operations to lead the team that handles regulatory requests and complaints, copyright notices, and sanctions screening and operations. 

We're looking for an excellent operations manager. You'll manage a team and own how the work gets done: the queues, the systems, the operating model, and the outsourced partners who extend the team. The work is both high volume and high consequence. Some of these processes are established and need to scale. Others are still being built. Volumes are growing quickly across all of them, so you'll be running today's queues while designing the systems that will carry the next stage of growth. Claude is central to that plan, and you'll decide where it can take on the work and where people need to stay involved.

You'll work closely with our Regulatory Programs team as well as other I&C teams, who own the design and management of our regulatory and compliance programs. Your team runs the operations that put those programs into practice, working to the policy and standards those teams set. You'll also partner with Legal, Safeguards, Threat Intelligence, Engineering, and Support.

postings.location: San Francisco, CA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. The Corporate Network Engineering team owns Anthropic's corporate network: the wired, wireless, and edge infrastructure in our offices and research facilities around the world, and the standards, management systems, and telemetry that let a small team run them. We hold that network to the bar of a production service — designed for failure, managed as code, observable end-to-end, and secure by default — while delivering reliable connectivity to the people who depend on it every day.

You'll set the technical direction together with your engineers and own the final decision on it and on the architecture standards, review and guide designs and the hard trade-offs, and lead vendor and platform decisions. You'll lead and grow a small team of network engineers: set priorities, drive decisions to closure, hire, and develop people. The team is small and the scope is broad, so this role needs real depth in campus and edge networking, judgment about what to standardize, automate, buy, and build, and the range to go from a wiring-closet decision to a budget defense in the same afternoon.

You'll report to the head of IT Engineering and partner closely with our Buildouts, AV, and Endpoint teams; with Security Engineering on network security, authentication, and detections; with Physical Security, whose systems are critical for protecting Anthropic employees and depend on a reliable network; with Workplace, Real Estate, Procurement, and external logistics and integration partners on new site buildouts; and with our production networking teams, whose bar for reliability and automation is the one we hold ourselves to. Your work will directly shape how we scale to AI Safety Level 4 and beyond.

Responsibilities

- Lead and grow the Corporate Network Engineering team — hiring, development, performance, planning, and prioritization

- Set technical direction with the team and own the final call on architecture standards across edge, campus switching, wireless, segmentation, out-of-band management, and telemetry; review designs and risky changes, and step in on the hard problems

- Own reliability and operations: monitoring people act on, incident response and post-incident reviews that produce changes, an on-call and escalation model a small team can sustain, change safety, and lifecycle currency

- Move the fleet toward network-as-code: templated configuration with change control, staged rollouts, drift detection, and automation that removes operational toil

- Partner with Security Engineering and Detection & Response on network authentication, segmentation, and the network as a detection source

- Deliver networks for new offices and research facilities and upgrade existing sites through live migrations — with Buildouts, AV, Physical Security, Workplace, Real Estate, and our logistics partners — while keeping interruptions to employees minimal

- Own vendor, carrier, and integrator relationships and the network hardware budget: evaluations, contracts, lead times, and multi-year refresh

- Have 10+ years designing, building, and operating enterprise campus and edge networks, including at least one environment with dozens of sites across regions

- Have 5+ years leading engineers, including at least 3 years as a people manager

- Default to the secure design, then do the creative work to make it painless for the people using it — and can walk an executive or an engineer through the trade-off and make a recommendation

- Have run the operational side, not just designed it: out-of-band access, monitoring people act on, an on-call model a small team can sustain, and change safety

- Are pragmatic about what to build, buy, or automate, have run vendor evaluations with real money at stake, and chase problems across organizational boundaries to the actual root cause

- Communicate clearly with engineers, executives, contractors, and landlords, and can bring a room of senior engineers with strong opinions to a decision they'll commit to

- Have led corporate networking at a company that added offices faster than it added network engineers

- Have implemented certificate-based network authentication (802.1X/EAP-TLS or equivalent) and identity- or device-based segmentation at scale

- Have shipped network configuration as code and built telemetry pipelines that security and support teams actually use

- Have designed dense wireless for large event spaces and high-occupancy floors

- Have been through multiple office builds with real estate and construction teams — including networks that physical security systems depend on — and know what to ask for before the walls close

- Have managed integrators, MSPs, or smart-hands providers as an extension of a small team while keeping design authority in-house

- Enterprise edge: firewalls and routing (HA design, routing protocols, policy management across a fleet)

- Campus switching and high-density enterprise wireless (L2/L3 design, redundancy, RF design, 6 GHz, high-density venues)

- Segmentation and access control (certificate-based 802.1X, dynamic segmentation, guest and IoT isolation)

- Out-of-band management and secure, auditable administrative access

- Network observability (streaming telemetry, flow and log pipelines)

- Physical infrastructure for buildouts (MDF/IDF design, structured cabling, power and cooling, carrier and path diversity)

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. Review technical architectures and code produced by your FDEs, ensuring the team ships high-quality, production-ready solutions that solve real customer problems.

Build repeatable playbooks, starter repositories, integration templates, and an internal knowledge base that captures what your team learns in the field.

Partner with Product and Engineering to translate field insights into product improvements. Serve as the voice of the customer in internal planning.

Travel to customer sites as needed (25-50%), particularly during engagement kickoffs and for your team's highest-priority accounts.

10+ years of experience in software engineering, solutions architecture, or a technical customer-facing role such as forward deployed engineering or consulting.

2+ years of people management experience within a services/post-sales/FDE organization with a track record of hiring, developing, and retaining strong engineers.

Experience building organizations from 0->1, not just inheriting an existing one.

Experience working directly with enterprise customers on technical implementations, including comfort navigating complex organizational dynamics.

Executive presence with the ability to move fluidly between strategic conversations with senior stakeholders and hands-on debugging sessions with engineers.

Strong written and verbal communication skills. You can translate technical complexity into clear narratives for diverse audiences.

Genuine excitement about building something new and defining what great looks like for a team that doesn't yet exist.

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. postings.location: San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Anthropic is seeking a Manager, Infrastructure Capex Accounting to join our Infrastructure Accounting team. In this role, you will execute day-to-day accounting for Anthropic's owned infrastructure assets — the GPUs, networking equipment, and data center buildouts underpinning our recently announced $50bn investment in American computing infrastructure. As we continue our rapid growth, you will help ensure the operational scalability and financial accuracy of the core functions that enable Anthropic's research and commercial success.

This is an opportunity to be at the heart of one of the fastest-scaling companies in the industry, and to shape how Anthropic's growing fixed asset base is accounted for and understood across the business.

You will own end-to-end accounting for Anthropic's capex and fixed asset portfolio, working closely with cross-functional partners across Data Center Operations, Finance, and Legal. You'll apply deep technical accounting expertise under ASC 360, and help build the processes, controls, and systems that let this function scale.

Responsibilities

- Own end-to-end accounting for Anthropic's AI infrastructure capex and fixed asset portfolio, including monthly close, construction-in-progress (CIP) tracking, reconciliations, roll-forwards, and flux analysis

- Apply technical accounting expertise to complex infrastructure arrangements under ASC 360 (capitalization, useful lives, impairment, disposals, and asset retirement obligations)

- Partner with Data Center Operations, Legal, and Finance teams during contract negotiation and execution to ensure accounting implications are understood before commitments are made

- Serve as a trusted finance partner to non-finance stakeholders — explaining the financial statement impact of their decisions in clear, simple terms they can act on

- Collaborate cross-functionally to improve the quality of upstream data pipelines from operational and contract systems, particularly around asset receipt, deployment, and in-service dates

- Help design and scale systems, processes, and controls to support a rapidly growing fixed asset portfolio

- Collaborate with and mentor junior accounting professionals across the Infrastructure Accounting team
