Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

As part of our growing Data Science and Analytics team, you will play an instrumental role in our company’s mission of building safe and beneficial artificial intelligence by driving data-informed decision making across our organization. You bring experience from high-bar teams and are eager to help shape the norms and best practices of a growing data science team as Anthropic continues to scale. In this unique company, technology, and moment in history, your work will be critical to informing our strategy as we deploy safe, frontier AI at scale to the world.

You’ll be the senior data science leader embedded in our Developer Platform product team and a strategic thought partner to its product leads. You’ll help set product direction for the Claude Developer Platform, spanning our core API, agent orchestration, tool and MCP integrations, and knowledge management capabilities. You’ll bring a point of view on where to invest, how to grow our platform business, and how to deliver more value for the developers and enterprises building on Claude. As a tech lead manager, you’ll also manage a small team of Product Data Scientists, setting their agenda and raising the bar for how data shapes product decisions.

Responsibilities:

- Act as a strategic thought partner to Developer Platform product leads, helping shape product strategy, roadmap priorities, and the major bets the team makes

- Set the data science agenda for Developer Platform, deciding where the Product Data Science team can have the most impact and what it should deprioritize

- Manage and develop a small team of Product Data Scientists, coaching them to move from answering questions to shaping decisions

- Frame the most important and ambiguous questions facing the platform, from how developers and enterprises adopt it to how AI agents are being built and deployed at scale, size the opportunities, and make clear recommendations, including when they challenge the current direction

- Define how Developer Platform measures success, establishing the core metrics and measurement frameworks that align teams and leadership on what matters

- Set the standard for experimentation and causal inference across Developer Platform, including where API and B2B products make clean experiments hard, and personally lead the highest-stakes analyses

- Turn complex analyses into clear narratives and recommendations that drive decisions with senior leadership and cross-functional partners, including go-to-market teams

- Establish foundational data practices and shape the analytics infrastructure Developer Platform needs to support rapid iteration and decision-making as our products grow

You may be a good fit if you:

- Have extensive experience in data science, including leading analytics for a product area at significant scale

- Have 3+ years managing data science teams, including setting team direction and developing senior data scientists

- Have been a trusted partner to senior product and business leaders on API or developer-facing products, with clear examples of changing a roadmap or high-stakes decision

- Bring strong product sense and business judgment for developer and B2B products, including the ability to frame the right question and take a position with incomplete information

- Have deep expertise in experimental design, causal inference, and statistical modeling at high scale, with enough fluency in Python and SQL to stay hands-on and guide others’ technical work

- Communicate clearly in writing and in presentations, including to executive audiences

- Have a bias for action and thrive in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where you must create clarity and drive progress

- Care about the company’s mission of building helpful, honest, and harmless AI

- Strong candidates may also have:

- Experience with AI/ML products, large language models, or developer tools in the AI/ML ecosystem

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.
Annual Salary:
$460,000—$460,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Claude Code is changing how engineering organizations build software, and most of them need someone to show them how. That's you.

Technical Architects help customers get real work done with Claude Code, Claude Tag (Claude Code as an agent in Slack), and the enterprise admin controls that decide whether a rollout succeeds. You'll teach customers, partners and Anthropic's own field teams. Just as important, you'll train the trainers who carry that knowledge to everyone else.

We're hands-on AI engineers who would rather teach than sell. You'll work alongside customer engineering organizations, teaching them about Claude Code and shepherding rollouts with advanced admin knowledge. Most weeks you're in front of an audience with Claude Desktop or a terminal open: thousands of engineers on a public webinar one day, a customer's platform team in their own conference room the next week, office hours in between. The prep material often reaches you the day before.

The team is growing quickly this year, scope will grow as new products ship, and the people who join now will shape how it works.

Responsibilities

- 

Teach in every format. Take a standing rotation on Anthropic's public webinars in front of thousands of engineers at a time. Lead workshops and multi-day onsites, in person and virtual, built around a customer's own codebase and questions. Host office hours and multi-week cohorts where engineers, partners, and account teams bring live problems.

- 

Teach the teachers. Run train-the-trainer programs for customer technologists and champions, and certify them to deliver Anthropic's material.

- 

Empower admins. Educate enterprise admins on the technical requirements for a strong rollout by guiding them through single sign-on, permissions, connectors, spend controls, data-handling policy, and other advanced topics.

- 

Build fast with Claude. Turn a request into a polished deck, demo repository or plugin within a day, using the tools you teach. Explore new features the day they ship. Pick up a teammate's material and deliver it as if you wrote it.

- 

Bring field signal back to product. Tell the Claude Code, Claude Tag and Cowork teams what customers run into, specifically enough that they can fix it.

- 

Be the technical voice in the room. Partner with account executives, customer success managers, Applied AI Architects, support engineers and partner leads.

- 

Travel. Expect 30 to 50%, in bursts around onsites, workshops and events.

You may be a good fit if you have

- 

5+ years as a software engineer, solutions architect, developer advocate or similar. You still ship code and regularly teach engineering audiences.

- 

Current engineering range. You've shipped code other people depend on. You can go deep with a senior engineer anywhere in the stack. You use Claude Code or a similar agentic tool every day and have opinions about it.

- 

Big-stage presence. You've held large live audiences. You sound practiced with material you got that morning, and a broken demo doesn’t faze you.

- 

Range in one conversation. You can go from banter to a rigorous design discussion, and both feel natural.

- 

Care for people. You do right by a struggling customer, and you won't leave a confused room behind.

- 

Initiative. You build things without waiting for permission, and you say when an idea is half-formed, including your manager's.

- 

Steadiness when priorities shift, timelines are short and colleagues are under pressure.

- 

Comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving industry and product suite.

- 

A stake in safe AI. You care that large organizations deploy AI responsibly, and you want to help them do it.

- 

You love being on the frontier. You want to work at the edge of what’s possible and help define what comes next.

Strong candidates may also have

- 

Depth in enterprise identity and security review (SAML, OIDC, SCIM, SOC 2, HIPAA).

- 

Experience running Claude on Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Vertex AI.

- 

Time with regulated industries or with systems-integrator partners.

- 

A public record of technical teaching: talks, courses, videos or writing.

- 

An interest outside technology you can talk about with the same energy.

Responsabilités

- Superviser la découverte technique : cartographier les flux de travail clients, identifier les contraintes, définir le périmètre MVP et façonner l'architecture de la solution pour les déploiements d'agents personnalisés.

- Diriger l'exécution et la livraison des travaux d'ingénierie au quotidien au sein des équipes d'Anthropic et des clients. Assurer l'avancée des projets de manière fluide et séquencée. Effectuer des compromis en temps réel sur la portée et la priorité afin de préserver le chemin critique.

- Garantir la portée des produits pour les missions sur le terrain : définir le MVP, rédiger la documentation des exigences, prioriser le backlog d’ingénierie et gérer le périmètre par rapport aux critères de succès à mesure que les exigences évoluent.

Prenez en charge la relation client tout au long de la livraison. Organiser des briefings exécutifs, gérer les communications avec les parties prenantes concernant les responsables techniques et l'approvisionnement et représenter Anthropic auprès des hauts responsables commerciaux et techniques en termes de crédibilité technique.

Maîtriser la mesure de la valeur et du ROI : définir les hypothèses d'impact, établir les bases de référence et les indicateurs clés de performance, effectuer des mesures avant et après le déploiement et communiquer les résultats aux commanditaires exécutifs.

Codifier des modèles de solutions réutilisables, des cadres d'évaluation et des manuels techniques. Consigner les bonnes pratiques des différentes interactions et transmettre les signaux du terrain aux équipes Produit et Recherche afin d'améliorer notre plateforme et nos modèles.

Naviguer dans la complexité des entreprises et des réglementations : audits de sécurité, approbations juridiques, processus d'approvisionnement, exigences de conformité et dynamique organisationnelle.

Gérer la portée et le changement : gérer l'évolutivité des exigences, définir les attentes, négocier les modifications de contrats, identifier les risques en amont et les signaler avec un contexte clair, le cas échéant.

Gérer les opérations de livraison : cérémonies de sprint, revue des étapes et rapports d'avancement.

Se rendre sur les sites des clients pour nouer des relations, débloquer les livraisons et accélérer l'adoption (objectif de 25 à 50 %).

Profil recherché

- Pus de 5 ans d'expérience en leadership technique auprès des clients. Cela peut concerner la gestion de l'engagement technique, la gestion de programmes techniques ou la gestion de produits techniques, les fondateurs/startups, les profils techniques connexes, les services professionnels, le conseil ou les logiciels d'entreprise.

- Avoir mis en production des solutions agentiques basées sur l'IA, le ML ou le LLM. Vous comprenez les modèles applicables aux solutions, les approches d'intégration et les réalités du terrain.

- Vous êtes capable de mener des discussions sur l'architecture avec les parties prenantes de l'ingénierie, d'évaluer les compromis techniques et de tester les décisions techniques sous pression. Vous n'écrirez pas de code de production, mais serez responsable de la direction technique des engagements aux côtés des ingénieurs déployés sur le terrain (FDE).

Vous avez une expérience de la réalisation de projets techniques complexes et à fort enjeu pour des entreprises clientes, dont les résultats dépendent d'une coordination étroite et d'une prise de décision rapide, idéalement dans le cadre d'activités multiples au sein de secteurs réglementés.

Vous avez une personnalité affirmée : vous êtes à l’aise, crédible et capable de représenter Anthropic auprès des hauts dirigeants dans des environnements à forts enjeux.

Vous surmontez les contextes ambigus et apportez une structure là où il n'y en a pas.

Vous avez une mentalité de bâtisseur : vous êtes ici pour créer une fonction, pas pour l'occuper.

Atouts supplémentaires

- Expérience dans le domaine des services financiers, des soins de santé, des sciences de la vie ou de l'industrie pharmaceutique.

- Expérience dans une société d'ingénierie déployée sur le terrain ou dans des sociétés de services professionnels et de conseil.

- Compréhension exceptionnelle des capacités et des limites des LLM.

- Expérience avec les industries réglementées et les exigences de conformité.

- Expérience de la gestion d'équipes de livraison avec des ingénieurs intégrés sur les sites des clients.

- Familiarité avec les frameworks d'agents IA, les modèles d'utilisation d'outils et les architectures d'orchestration.

postings.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Anthropic’s Inference organization serves Claude to millions of users and enterprise customers, across our own products and the world’s largest cloud platforms, with the speed, reliability, and efficiency that frontier AI demands. The stack that makes this possible is deep and tightly coupled: accelerator kernels, an in-house inference engine that manages the entire token path for both production and research workloads, distributed routing, autoscaling, and capacity management. Every layer affects the others, often in ways that are hard to see in isolation. We build across GPUs, TPUs, and Trainium, and the complexity of building, testing, and shipping inference software grows with every platform we add.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive the programs that scale it. The work spans four closely coupled areas:

- 

Scaling and infrastructure. Routing, autoscaling, and capacity management for the serving fleet, and bringing new capacity online.

- 

Velocity. The toolchains, development environments, and CI/CD that let inference engineers build, test, and ship across every accelerator platform.

- 

Inference engine. The software between the accelerator kernels and the routing layer that serves every request.

- 

Performance. Improving throughput, latency, cost, and reliability across the stack, with correctness treated as part of performance.

This is not a status-tracking role. You'll own outcomes end to end, often where no single team is accountable for the whole picture. Much of your value comes from crossing boundaries into Research, Safeguards, Security, Compute, Infrastructure, API, and our cloud and silicon partners, and bringing back the requirements and dependencies that no team sees from inside its own space. There is little process to inherit, and we want to keep it that way: you'll build the minimum machinery the work needs and remove it when it stops helping. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a collaborator. We expect TPMs on this team to push hard on what AI-assisted program management and fleet operations can look like.

Key responsibilities

- 

Own the programs that scale Claude’s serving fleet across accelerator and cloud platforms, from early direction through delivery.

- 

Drive new capacity online end to end, working across compute, infrastructure, security, networking, and inference teams so one person is accountable for the whole path.

- 

Build visibility into supply, demand, and utilization with capacity and finance partners, and drive trade-offs among utilization, cost, latency, and reliability to a clear decision.

- 

Lead reliability programs and large migrations without disrupting production traffic or research, and make sure incident follow-ups land in team roadmaps.

- 

Drive the programs that make inference engineers faster: define the productivity metrics that matter, find the bottlenecks, and improve how software is built, tested, and released across platforms, in step with Anthropic’s central Infrastructure org.

- 

Coordinate roadmaps and priorities across the production, research, and safeguards needs that depend on the same teams.

- 

Track performance and efficiency work from opportunity to measured impact in production, with correctness held as a release criterion.

- 

Own inference readiness for model launches alongside our launch TPMs.

Minimum qualifications

- 

7+ years of experience as a TPM, or in an equivalent engineering or SRE lead role, owning large multi-team infrastructure programs end to end in production distributed systems, ML infrastructure, or cloud platforms. You can speak to the outcomes in detail, including where a program slipped and what you did about it.

- 

Technical fluency in large-scale serving infrastructure, including request routing and load balancing, autoscaling, capacity planning, cluster orchestration, deployment and rollout, and observability. You know enough to challenge a design, find the real risk, and add value beyond tracking.

- 

A working understanding of how LLM inference uses hardware (prefill and decode, batching, caching, compute versus memory bandwidth versus interconnect), or a track record of getting deep in an unfamiliar technical domain quickly.

- 

A track record of building program mechanisms from scratch on ambiguous, fast-moving efforts, and of retiring process that has stopped earning its keep.

- 

The ability to drive outcomes across organizations you don't manage, with competing priorities and unclear decision ownership. You read people and rooms well, know when to push and when to listen, and earn the trust of senior engineers and researchers.

- 

Strong written communication, including plans, reviews, and executive updates that many teams depend on.

- 

Low ego and high ownership. You do whatever the program needs, whether that is writing a script, running an incident bridge, or chasing a quota, and you care more about the outcome than about scope or credit.

- 

Care about Anthropic's mission and about serving frontier AI safely and reliably.

Preferred qualifications

- 

Direct experience with LLM or ML inference serving at scale, such as model servers, batching and scheduling, KV caching, quantization, speculative decoding, or multi-model routing.

- 

Experience with accelerator infrastructure (GPU, TPU, or Trainium), including cluster bring-up, hardware qualification, or running one workload across more than one accelerator platform.

- 

Experience managing capacity across multiple clouds or regions, including demand forecasting, headroom policy, cost modeling, or unit economics for compute-heavy services.

- 

Experience with developer productivity, release engineering, or CI/CD at scale, especially for hardware-dependent workloads, and with using engineering metrics to measurably raise velocity.

- 

Experience running performance or efficiency programs, with enough grounding in rooflines, kernels, ML compilers (XLA, Triton, Neuron), numerics, or collective communication to reason about trade-offs with the engineers doing the work.

- 

Familiarity with Kubernetes-based orchestration and job scheduling.

- 

Experience working with research teams and turning their needs into infrastructure requirements.

- 

Practical experience using AI tools in your own workflow, including building automations or agents, and clear ideas about where they help and where they don't.

postings.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
postings.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the Role

Safeguards Engineering builds and operates the infrastructure that keeps Anthropic's AI systems safe in production — the classifiers, detection pipelines, evaluation platforms, and monitoring systems that sit between our models and the real world. That infrastructure needs to be not just correct, but reliable: when a safety-critical pipeline goes down or degrades, the consequences can be serious, and they can be invisible until someone looks closely.

As a Technical Program Manager for Safeguards Infrastructure and Evals, you'll own the operational health and forward momentum of this stack. Your primary responsibility is driving reliability — owning the incident-response and post-mortem process, ensuring SLOs are defined and met in partnership with various teams, and making sure that when things go wrong, the right people know, the right actions get taken, and those actions actually get closed out. Alongside that ongoing operational rhythm, you'll coordinate the larger platform investments: migrations, eval-platform improvements, and the cross-team dependencies that connect them.

This role sits at the intersection of operations and program management. It requires genuine technical depth — you need to understand how these systems work well enough to triage effectively, judge what's actually safety-critical versus what can wait, and have informed conversations with the engineers building and maintaining them. But the core of the job is keeping the machine running well and the work moving.

What You'll Do:

- Own the Safeguards Engineering ops review - Drive the recurring cadence that keeps the team informed and coordinated: surfacing recent incidents and failures, bringing visibility to reliability trends, and making sure the right people are in the room when decisions need to be made. This is the heartbeat of how Safeguards Eng stays ahead of operational risk.

- Drive incident tracking and post-mortem execution - When incidents happen — and in this space, they happen regularly — you'll make sure they get followed through properly. That means tracking incidents across the organization (including those owned by partner teams like Inference), ensuring post-mortems get written, and most critically, making sure the action items that come out of them actually get done. Closing the loop on post-mortem actions is one of the highest-leverage things this role does.

- Establish and maintain SLOs with partner teams - Work with Safeguards Engineering teams and key partners — particularly Inference and Cloud Inference — to define service-level objectives for safety-critical pipelines. Then build the tracking and reporting that makes it possible to tell whether those SLOs are being met, and surface it when they're not.

- Maintain runbook quality and incident-ownership clarity - Safety-critical systems need clear playbooks for when things go wrong. Partner with engineering leads to keep runbooks accurate, actionable, and up to date — and ensure that ownership of incidents is unambiguous so that nothing falls through the cracks during an active incident.

- Drive platform migrations and infrastructure projects - Own the program management for the larger infrastructure work on the roadmap: migrating the infra from one platform to the next, moving from one incident platform to the next and from one cloud system monitoring to another, and other migrations as they come. These are cross-team efforts with real dependencies — your job is to keep them sequenced, on track, and connected to the teams that need them.

- Coordinate evals platform improvements - Partner with the evals engineering team to drive improvements to the evaluation platform — including self-serve capabilities and the broader eval factory infrastructure. Help scope the work, track dependencies on other Safeguards systems, and make sure the evals platform is keeping pace with the team's needs.

You might be a good fit if you:

- Have solid technical program management experience, particularly in operational or infrastructure-heavy environments — you're comfortable owning a mix of ongoing operational cadences and discrete project work simultaneously.

- Understand how production ML systems work well enough to triage incidents intelligently and have substantive conversations with engineers about what's going wrong and why — you don't need to write the code, but you need to follow the technical thread.

- Are energized by closing loops. Post-mortem action items that never get done, SLOs that no one checks, runbooks that go stale — these things bother you, and you know how to build the processes and follow-ups that fix them.

- Can work effectively across team boundaries — comfortable coordinating with partner teams (like Inference) where you don't have direct authority, and skilled at keeping shared work moving through influence and clear communication.

- Thrive in environments where the work shifts between "keep the lights on" and "build something new" — and can context-switch between incident follow-ups and longer-horizon platform projects without dropping either.

- Have experience with or strong interest in AI safety — you understand why the reliability of a safety-critical pipeline is a different kind of problem than the reliability of a product feature, and that distinction motivates you.

Strong candidates may also:

- Have experience with SRE practices, incident management frameworks, or on-call operations at scale.

- Have worked on or with evaluation infrastructure for ML systems — understanding how evals get designed, run, and interpreted.

- Have experience driving infrastructure migrations in complex, multi-team environments — particularly where the migration touches operational systems that can't go offline.

- Be familiar with monitoring and alerting tooling (PagerDuty, Datadog, or equivalents) and the operational culture around them.

Reporting to the Director of Global Accounts Payable, you will be the single point of accountability for who our vendors are and get paid: onboarding, bank-detail verification, supporting documentation vetting, data quality and the controls around all of it. Anthropic's vendor base is growing quickly across the US, Europe and Asia-Pacific, and a clean, verified vendor data is what keeps a fast-growing company scale with the necessary controls. 

This role is deliberately separate from invoice processing and payments. You will control vendor records and bank details; you will not book invoices or move money. That separation is the point of the role, and you will own the SOX controls that enforce it and help design the access model that keeps it that way.

This is an opportunity to build a vendor-master function from the ground up and leverage process automation with Claude while supporting the team making AI safe.

Responsibilities

Supplier onboarding

- 

Run intake for every new vendor and payee: validate completeness, collect and verify supporting documentation, and enable records in the ERP backbone system against agreed service levels

- 

Validate supporting documents; set 1099-reportable and tax flags correctly

- 

Confirm third-party risk and restricted-party screening before activation

- 

Set up one-time and non-vendor payees with the right record type rather than forcing them through full onboarding

- 

Partner with TPRM and IA teams on control requirements and continuous process improvement 

- 

1099 annual reporting 

Bank details and fraud prevention

- 

Own every bank-detail setup and change; validate against a bank letter on letterhead or an approved equivalent (void checks, etc.)

- 

Run independent callbacks per policy using contact details sourced independently of the request, and record the evidence

- 

Validate international bank formats and addresses (IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, ABA, SEPA, BSB, IFSC, Japanese bank/branch codes)

- 

Identify and escalate business-email-compromise attempts and other payment-fraud red flags

Data quality and maintenance

- 

Maintain vendor structure: parent/child and remit-to relationships, entity and country records, contacts and payment terms

- 

Lead vendor consolidation: eliminate duplicate vendors and bank accounts, execute merges and inactivations in batched, logged, reviewed changes

- 

Run periodic health reviews for dormant vendors, stale bank letters, missing tax forms and incomplete records; drive 1099 and TIN readiness for year-end

- 

Own periodic vendor deactivation campaigns

Controls and audit

- 

Own the vendor-master SOX controls as the named control owner: maker-checker on every create and change, change-log review, evidence retained on every record

- 

Prepare the periodic review of bank-detail changes paid, and address Internal Audit and external auditor requests

- 

Partner with Finance Systems to design and maintain ERP security roles so vendor master, invoicing and payments stay separated

- 

Flag any suspicious vendor set-up activity through the appropriate channels

Process, systems and improvement

- 

Own vendor-master documentation, intake checklists, requester guidance and service levels

- 

Serve as the vendor-data expert through process migrations, including data conversion and post-migration fixes

- 

Partner on automation: AI-assisted intake validation, document extraction, bank-format checks and a vendor self-service portal

- 

Report monthly on onboarding volume, cycle time, bank changes, exceptions and data quality, and use the data to improve the process

Minimum qualifications

- 7+ years in vendor master or AP operations with 3+ years of ownership

- 

Owned a vendor master in an ERP end to end — process, controls and data — across multiple entities and countries

- 

Hands-on experience verifying bank details and preventing payment fraud: bank letters, independent callbacks, BEC red flags, international bank formats

- 

Experience with vendor tax documentation: W-9/W-8 validation, TIN matching, VAT/GST IDs, 1099 flagging

- 

Working knowledge of procure-to-pay controls — segregation of duties, maker-checker, change logs, audit evidence — and have performed or owned a SOX control

- 

Led a vendor data cleanup, consolidation or ERP migration and can show the outcome

- 

The confidence to hold the line with requesters, vendors and senior stakeholders under time pressure while staying clear and helpful

- 

Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills with large datasets (dedupe, lookups, reconciliations) and exceptional attention to detail

Preferred qualifications

- 

Workday Financials vendor management, and experience with Zip, Coupa or a similar procure-to-pay platform

- 

SOX experience at a public company or one preparing to go public

- 

Experience supporting APAC and EMEA vendors in a high-growth, multi-entity company

- 

Experience designing or reviewing ERP security roles with a systems team

- 

Comfort using AI tools to automate validation, follow-ups and reporting
